documents.title: Capper removal
documents.summary: Take the capper turret, column and inner shaft off an EXACTA-R so the main bearing and bushings can be replaced.
safety: Lock out the machine and release air before you start. The upper head is heavy: lift it straight up with straps spaced evenly, or it will stick and can swing.
Support the bull gear with lumber or bottle jacks before you remove the inner shaft.
tools: Crossbar for lifting the inner shaft

steps.title: Prepare and mark everything
text: Remove all change parts, including chucks, starwheels and guides. Remove the bridge section if it could be damaged. Disconnect the air lines and electrical cables that run to the slip ring on top of the capper.
Mark the upper turret against the keyways, the carousel plate with the head numbers, and the bull gear against the starwheels in case they drop.
Lower the capper turret to the MIN elevation on the HMI Elevation page. Measure the bridge plate height and the capper height so you can reassemble to the same position.
steps.caption: Capper column before removal

steps.title: Remove the gearbox
text: Remove the bolt that retains the gearbox, then the belt and tensioner pulley. Remove the gearbox and check the gearbox and key for wear.
steps.caption: Capper gearbox

steps.title: Remove the upper column keys
text: Remove the two outer keys from the upper turret shaft.
steps.caption: Upper column keys

steps.title: Lift off the capper head
text: With the lifting screw still in place, lift the upper head with a forklift. Space the straps evenly around the carousel and keep clear of the bridge.
You can also run the head off the end of the jack screw with the height control, as long as the forklift supports it and follows it up.

callouts.label: Refit
callouts.text: Lower the head until it touches the jack screw, then use the height control to engage the threads and bring it to height.

steps.caption: Lifting the capper head

steps.title: Inspect the lifting screw
text: Remove the lifting screw by hand and check the threads on the brass nut. Replace the nut or the screw if either is damaged.
If the carousel will not come off, lift the head about 30 in, enough to clear the column plus the jack screw, and block it with lumber.
steps.caption: Lifting screw and brass nut

steps.title: Support the bull gear
text: Mark where the bull gear sits relative to the starwheels. Support it with lumber or bottle jacks before going further.
steps.caption: Bull gear supported

steps.title: Remove the column base ring
text: Remove the brass ring on top of the shaft. It should not touch the outer shaft. Loosen or remove the two anti-rotation bolts or set screws that hold the inner column, then remove the base ring.
steps.caption: Brass ring and anti-rotation bolts

steps.title: Lift out the inner column and castle
text: The inner shaft has alignment keys. Mark the keyways on the plate before removal to make refitting easier. Fix a crossbar to the shaft and pull the column straight up.
Mark the castle position on the base plate and remove the castle. Keep the leveling shims.
steps.caption: Castle on the base plate

steps.title: Remove the inner shaft
text: The inner shaft is held at the bottom by an iron ring connected to the drive gear and the outer column. Remove the top ring and base ring, then lift the shaft out.
steps.caption: Inner shaft

steps.title: Replace the main bearing and bushings
text: Remove the bolts that hold the rotating disk to the bull gear. Strap the disk and lift it straight up. The main support hub keeps the outer race and the bottom bearing.
Replace the bearings and both bushings, one at the top of the main column and one at the bottom. Replace dust covers and brushes as needed.

callouts.label: Tip
callouts.text: The main bearing is greased from a port on the front of the machine, but pre-greasing it on assembly makes sure it starts with enough lubricant.

steps.caption: Capper main bearing

documents.title: Scroll U-joint assembly
documents.summary: Assemble the infeed scroll drive U-joint with both yokes in the same plane so the scroll turns smoothly.
safety: Lock out the machine before working on the scroll drive.
tools: Hex keys for the set screws

hero.text: **Key point:** both end yokes must be aligned in the same plane. If they are out of phase the scroll speeds up and slows down on every turn.
hero.caption: Correct: both yokes in the same plane

steps.title: Check yoke orientation
text: Make sure both end yokes are in the same plane. Use the fork ears and the factory marks as your reference.
steps.caption: Incorrect: yokes not in the same plane

steps.title: Rotate one end if needed
text: Turn one end of the joint on the splined shaft until the two yokes line up.

steps.title: Mark the position
text: Mark the spline position so you can separate the two halves to fit them on the 90 degree gearbox and the scroll mount.

steps.title: Install the joint
text: Fit the joint in the machine and tighten the two set screws on each end.

steps.title: Run and confirm
text: Run the machine and confirm the U-joint shaft turns smoothly, with no surge or vibration.

documents.title: Centerlining
documents.summary: The five settings, in order, that put a filler and capper back on its centerline after a changeover or a crash.

meta.Area: Filler, conveyors, scroll, stars, capper, reject

safety: Jog the machine in manual mode only, and keep guards closed while it moves.

steps.title: Head 1 filling position
text: Set every bottle lifting platform level (within 1 mm) with the dead plate on the infeed side of the lifting cam, section A.
Place a bottle in section B of the cam. If it is too far left or right, adjust the infeed star. If it is too far forward or back, adjust the lifting cam.
Jog the bottle out of section C and set the filler height: no more than 1 mm compression for cone nozzles, or 6 mm clearance for inverted cone nozzles.

callouts.label: Note
callouts.text: The lifting cam lowers the bottle gradually before it leaves the filling carousel for the central star.

steps.caption: Bottle lifting cam sections A, B and C

steps.title: Conveyors
text: Center the bottle on the conveyor, using the bottle seam if there is one.
Bring the front and back rails to 0.5 mm from the bottle, 1 mm in total (the thickness of a dime).
Set the upper rail above the middle of the bottle and the lower rail just above the bottom edge.

callouts.label: Tip
callouts.text: Shingling: close the rails a little. Sticking: open them slightly. For bad shingling use low-friction or roller rails.

steps.caption: Conveyor rails set to the bottle

steps.title: Infeed scroll
text: With a bottle centered on the conveyor, bring the scroll to 0.5 mm from it. If the scroll has a height adjustment, set it as close to the middle of the bottle as possible without touching the chain or the infeed star.
Adjust the rail forks so the scroll keeper opens and closes without hitting them. Center any change part here like a rail.
Time the scroll to the infeed star with a 10 mm wrench.

callouts.label: Watch
callouts.text: Bottles leaning forward means the conveyor is too slow. Leaning back means it is too fast. Fix the speed, not the rails.

steps.caption: Infeed scroll

steps.title: Central star and capper carousel
text: Put a bottle at the outfeed of the filling carousel and time the central star to it.
Jog the bottle into the capper carousel and adjust the neck guides so the bottle is not pinched and the cap lines up.
Adjust the outside guide or belt so the bottle is held through the torque zone.

callouts.label: Tip
callouts.text: The capper carousel is slotted. After a crash it can be retimed like a starwheel.

steps.caption: Central star neck guides

steps.title: Outfeed star and reject
text: Time the outfeed star to the capper carousel.
Align the reject bumper with the outside rail of the outfeed star, or the fingers with the reject lane.
Align the conveyor rails with the reject. They can narrow after the outfeed tunnel guard to keep control.

callouts.label: Spec
callouts.text: First reject finger: 35 mm from the outfeed star center with five fingers, 40 mm with six.

steps.caption: Outfeed star and reject

documents.title: Setting up the filler zero position
documents.summary: Line up head 1, the cam, the star and scroll, the two sensors and the encoder so the filler knows where zero is.
safety: Jog the machine in manual mode only. Lock out before loosening the cam, star or encoder.
tools: Drill with countersink (if no pointer mark exists)

hero.text: Work in this order: center the bottle under the valve, set the cam, star and scroll, then the head 1 sensor, the bottle presence sensor, and finally the encoder.
hero.caption: Zero position overview

steps.title: Center head 1
text: Rotate the filler until head 1 sits on the line between the center of the infeed star and the center of the filling carousel.
steps.caption: Head 1 between the star and carousel centers

steps.title: Set the cam, star and scroll
text: If the filling cam or infeed star is not aligned, set them now. Moving the cam moves the bottle toward or away from the carousel. Timing the star moves it along the direction of travel.
Then time the infeed scroll to the infeed star.
steps.caption: Filling cam and infeed star

steps.title: Position the head 1 sensor
text: Point the head 1 sensor at the first third of the reflector, in the direction of travel.
If there is no pointer mark, loosen the mechanical pointer and use it to mark the slip ring plate. Drill the mark with a countersink and fill it with paint marker.
steps.caption: Head 1 sensor and reflector

steps.title: Position the bottle presence sensor
text: Point the bottle presence photo eye at the center of the bottle in its pocket.
If bottles fill but do not reject properly, you can move it slightly leading or trailing, but it should otherwise always point at the bottle center.
steps.caption: Bottle presence photo eye

steps.title: Set the encoder to zero
text: Loosen the encoder lock collar and turn the encoder by hand until the HMI shows 0 degrees, then tighten the collar.

callouts.label: Tolerance
callouts.text: Tightening the collar can move the reading. Up to plus or minus 5 degrees is acceptable.

documents.title: Configuring Secomea SiteManager
documents.summary: Set the uplink and device agents on a Secomea SiteManager so Ronchi can reach the machine remotely.
safety: Agree the external network settings with the customer's IT team before you change the uplink.
tools: Laptop on the machine ethernet service port

steps.title: Install the Appliance Launcher
text: Download and install the Secomea Appliance Launcher on your laptop.

steps.title: Select the SiteManager
text: Connect to the machine ethernet service port, open the Appliance Launcher and pick the SiteManager from the list. Check that the MAC address matches the one printed on the device, then click Next.

steps.title: Set the machine network address
text: Enter the IP address the SiteManager will use on the machine network. It is in the electrical drawings, usually page 160. Click Next.

steps.title: Set the uplink
text: Enter the external access settings chosen by the customer and click Next. Click Next again to skip the secondary uplink.

steps.title: Point it at GateManager
text: Enter the GateManager address and domain token. Set the appliance name to the machine number and customer. Click Next.

steps.title: Save and reboot
text: Tick **Check here to preserve password** and click Save/Reboot.

steps.title: Open the SiteManager web page
text: With the laptop still on the service port, browse to the SiteManager address using **https://**. Without https the page will not load. If the browser warns the connection is not private, choose Advanced, then Proceed.
Log in as admin. Get the current password from the Ronchi service lead. It is not printed in this guide.

steps.title: Add the device agents
text: Click Edit for Device Agents. Add every device that needs remote access, including the DEV1 port.
Click Save, then Continue Setup.

steps.title: Log in
text: Open the SiteManager web page as in the steps above. If the factory password does not work, use the Ronchi commissioning password from the service lead.

steps.title: Change the uplink
text: Click Edit for the Uplink port and enter the customer's external access settings.

steps.title: Save
text: Click Save, then Continue Setup.

documents.title: Exporting camera footage from the machine
documents.summary: Save a clip from the machine's AXIS camera recorder to a USB stick from the HMI.

steps.title: Open the camera desktop
text: Press the video camera icon on the HMI bottom toolbar. When the Remote Desktop prompt appears, choose Yes.

steps.title: Start the camera system
text: Open **Axis Recorder Toolbox** at the top left of the desktop. On the welcome screen click **Start AXIS Camera System**.

steps.title: Open Recordings
text: Next to the camera tab at the top left, click **+** and choose **Recordings**.

steps.title: Mark the export area
text: Above the timeline on the right, click the two-flag **Export Area** button. A white band appears on the timeline. Drag its blue handles to the length you need. You need a mouse plugged into the back of the HMI for this.

steps.title: Export as MP4
text: Click **Export**, open **Advanced Settings** and set the format to **MP4**, then export.

steps.title: Copy the file
text: Open File Finder, then Documents. Exported files are named by date and time. Press and hold the file (or right-click) and copy it.

steps.title: Paste to USB
text: Remove the mouse and plug a USB stick into the back of the HMI. Minimize the camera program from the blue taskbar, select the USB drive in File Finder and paste the file.

steps.title: Eject the USB
text: Tap the up arrow at the bottom right of the HMI toolbar, choose the USB device and Eject. Remove the stick.

documents.title: Purge unit start-up
documents.summary: Start the Pepperl+Fuchs 6000 purge unit and energize a purged filler safely.
safety: The filler must not be powered until the purge cycle finishes. Never bypass the purge contactor.
All base frame doors and the electrical cabinet must be closed and bolted before you start.

hero.text: The purge unit pushes 4 to 5 volumes of clean air through the enclosures before it lets the filler power up. Opening a base door drops the purge contactor and shuts the filler down.
hero.caption: P+F 6000 purge unit

steps.title: Close and bolt the doors
text: Fit the base frame doors and tighten each bolt to the marked 35 in-lb. Make sure the electrical cabinet is bolted closed.
steps.caption: Base frame doors

steps.title: Turn on the air
text: Turn on air to the filler and to the purge unit.
Filler: 80 to 90 PSI. Purge unit: 50 to 60 PSI.
steps.caption: Purge air supply

steps.title: Switch on the filler main disconnect
text: Turn the QC main panel disconnect on the filler to ON.
steps.caption: Main panel disconnect

steps.title: Switch on the purge contactor panel
text: Turn the remote QP purge contactor panel disconnect to ON. The QP panel is behind the air conditioner on the main line electrical panel.
steps.caption: QP purge contactor panel

steps.title: Wait for the purge cycle
text: The purge unit powers up and runs the air exchange. Allow 30 to 40 minutes before the filler is energized.
steps.caption: Purge cycle running

steps.title: Test the purge
text: Open one base door. The QP contactor should drop out and shut the filler down. Close the door and let the purge cycle run again.

documents.title: Capper slip ring removal and upgrade to newer style
documents.summary: Remove the old capper slip ring and fit the newer style unit, including the changes the new unit needs.

meta.Area: Slip ring on top of the capper

safety: Power down, shut off the air and lock out the machine.
The slip ring weighs about 35 lb. Lift it with a second person.
tools: Cutting tool for the connecting plate
Small bracket for the new connector

hero.text: The newer style slip ring (right) is larger than the old one (left). Plan for the three modifications in this guide: a cut in the connecting plate, removal of the air fitting extensions, and a bracket for the new connector.
hero.caption: Old style (left) and new style (right)

steps.title: Disconnect the encoder
text: Unscrew the threaded encoder cable.

steps.title: Remove the gear covers and anti-rotation arms
text: Remove the 8 bolts and the bracket that join the two gear cover halves. Unbolt the anti-rotation arms.

steps.title: Disconnect air and wiring
text: Disconnect the air lines at the top of the slip ring. Unwire the two junction boxes that take wires from the slip ring. You can do this step earlier if it is easier.
steps.caption: Junction boxes wired from the slip ring

steps.title: Unbolt and lift out
text: Remove the 4 bolts that hold the unit to the upper capper plate. Lift the slip ring up, and before it is fully out disconnect the two air lines on its underside.

steps.title: Separate the gears
text: Remove the 4 bolts and the black box to separate the two gears. Keep the gear with the encoder; it goes on the new unit.

steps.title: Mount the encoder
text: Cut a section from the connecting plate so the new style cable fits through, then fit the encoder gear to the new unit.

steps.title: Fit the spacer hub
text: The new unit is larger. Remove its bottom plate to get the hub (it acts as a spacer) on, then place the unit.

steps.title: Remove the air fitting extensions
text: Remove the extensions on the air fittings under the old position. They stick out too far and stop the new unit seating on the upper plate.

steps.title: Mount the connector
text: The orange cable is too short to reach the new connector, so make a small bracket and bolt the connector to it.

steps.title: Route the power cable
text: The black power cable from the new connector does not go to the box on the anti-rotation arm. Feed it down the pipe with the other cables and air lines and wire it into box X22B.

steps.title: Reassemble and check SERCOS
text: Reassemble in reverse order. The black box removed earlier can go back on once the unit is on the turret plate.
Before power-up, check the wiring of the new RJ45 connector pin by pin.

callouts.label: Lesson learned
callouts.text: A miswired RJ45 connector on the new unit caused a SERCOS communication fault on first power-up.

documents.title: Inspecting and replacing the capper slip ring
documents.summary: Check the slip ring RJ45 wiring and shielding before you replace it, and fit a new pre-wired slip ring if you must.
safety: Lock out the machine before opening the slip ring terminal box.
tools: RJ45 crimp tool and spare male RJ45

blocks.heading: Check before you replace it
text: Most slip ring communication faults are wiring or shielding faults. Check all of these first.

steps.title: Check the RJ45 male connector
text: Check the wiring of the male RJ45.

steps.title: Check the RJ45 female connector
text: The female RJ45 is wired in the opposite order to the male. Check it against the male.

steps.title: Check the shield at the stripped end
text: At the base of the stripped part of the cable, the RJ45 shield must not touch the outer cable shield, not even with one stray strand.
Check both cables: the one from the slip ring into the terminal block and the one from the machine into the terminal block.

steps.title: Check the inner and outer shields
text: Cut back the black sheath. The outer shield (under a clear sheath) must not touch the inner shield (under the black sheath Ronchi adds).
steps.caption: These two shields must never touch

steps.title: Unpack the pre-wired unit
text: The new slip ring arrives already wired.

steps.title: Connect the female RJ45
text: Remove the grey plastic cover to fit the female RJ45 into the box. You can reuse the old plastic housing already in the box.

steps.title: Replace the male RJ45 if suspect
text: A spare male RJ45 is fixed to the cable, not yet wired. If you suspect the male connector, replace the machine-side RJ45 using the same colors as now. Remember the female is wired opposite to the male.

documents.title: Pump conveyor alignment
documents.summary: Centerline the pump conveyor chains and rails so pumps run through with 0.5 mm clearance and do not jam.
safety: Stop the machine before adjusting any assembly. Do not adjust rails while running production.

hero.text: Two chain conveyors and two rail guides control the pump. The chains can run together or separately for orientation, and each rail moves on its own. A third top rail is often fitted to stop shingling.
hero.caption: Pump conveyor

steps.title: Conveyor alignment
text: Slides the two chains closer or further apart to suit the width of the pump body. Fixed height in this example.

steps.title: Rail alignment
text: Slides the rails to suit the width of the gland nut. The height adjusts to suit gland nuts from different makers.

steps.title: Know the clearances
text: Rails in and out: 0.5 mm front and 0.5 mm back (B).
Gland nut rail up and down: 1.0 mm above the gland nut (A).
Top rail, if fitted: 1.0 mm above the pump (C).
steps.caption: Clearances A, B and C

steps.title: Loosen everything
text: Loosen all conveyor and rail alignment assemblies.

steps.title: Set the conveyors from the C-chute
text: Starting at the C-chute, set and tighten each conveyor assembly in turn, checking clearance with the largest pump on hand.

steps.title: Set the rails from the C-chute
text: Set and tighten the rail assemblies the same way, also starting at the C-chute. The pump must move freely with no rough transitions.

callouts.label: Rule
callouts.text: Always centerline in the direction of travel. Each change affects everything downstream. If a few adjustments during production do not fix it, stop and centerline from the start.

rows: Too much clearance to the rails or the chain. Close it up.
Look for hang-ups: loose hardware or sharp edges.
Pump stops, not tilted, nothing catching
Open the rail very slightly (0.5 mm) for larger pumps.
Jams entering or going down the S-chute (waterfall)
Add a top rail so pumps cannot ride over each other.

documents.title: Cap and pump sorter operation
documents.summary: How the disc sorter orients caps and pumps with air jets, how to set the orienting jets, and how to fix common faults.
safety: Keep hands out of the bowl while the disc is turning. Stop the sorter to clear jams.

hero.text: A large disc spins inside a stationary bowl. Plastic segments on the disc form pockets, and air jets blow the caps or pumps around until they drop into the pockets the right way up.
hero.caption: Disc sorter

blocks.heading: Air jet groups
text: Many machines also have one or two jets at the discharge to control parts as they leave.

rows: Clears parts that have not dropped into a pocket
Blows out any part not fully seated in its pocket
Clears loose parts before they reach the outfeed

blocks.heading: Air bank
text: On the air bank, regulators marked A, B and C match the three groups. Sections of the bank can run only with the self-cleaning jam door or whenever the sorter runs. Manual shut-off valves can switch sections on or off so one sorter can run different parts.
blocks.caption: Example air bank

blocks.heading: Set the orienting jets
text: The orienting jets work on the venturi effect. The side jet fills the part with air. The bottom jet pushes against that air. A wrong-way part is blown free, a right-way part stays in its pocket.

steps.title: Side jet off
text: Turn the side jet all the way down.

steps.title: Raise the bottom jet
text: With the sorter running, slowly turn the bottom jet up until every part blows out of its pocket.

steps.title: Raise the side jet
text: Turn the side jet up until good parts stay in the pocket and wrong-way parts are blown out.

rows: No parts coming into the sorter
Clean, check and reset the level photo eye.
Upside-down caps or wrong-way pumps leaving or jamming the disc
9 o'clock jets at maximum and cannot clear the disc
Speed up the sorter or slow the elevator.
Good parts blown out at 12 o'clock
Check the C-chute halves are aligned, and the sorter insert to the C-chute. If still jamming, raise the control jet slowly.

documents.title: Finding alarms in the filler PLC logic
documents.summary: Trace an HMI filler alarm (400 to 495) back to the logic that sets it in the filling PLC.
tools: Studio 5000 online or offline with the filling PLC program
FactoryTalk View project for the HMI

blocks.heading: How the alarms are mapped
bullets: All filling PLC alarms are numbered **400 to 495**.
The HMI triggers are **ALARMF_MESSAGE_0** to **ALARMF_MESSAGE_4**. They are 16-bit integers (machine PLC messages are 32-bit DINTs).
In the filling PLC they are **AlarF[0]** to **AlarF[4]**.
A COP instruction in routine **_35_Allarmi_Priorita_00_SET** copies the AlarF bits into the array **Alarm_Head**.
The alarms have no descriptions in the PLC, but **Alarm_Head[0].Pos[##]** matches the last two digits of the HMI alarm number.

blocks.heading: Worked example: alarm 477, filler phase error

steps.title: Find the message on the HMI
text: The message is in the HMI Alarms setup.

steps.title: Find the trigger tag
text: In the HMI Tags setup, ALARMF_MESSAGE_4 maps to AlarF[4] in the filling PLC. The PLC_FILL connection is set up in FactoryTalk Linx.

steps.title: Follow the COP
text: In the controller tags, AlarF[4] is used in the COP instruction in _35_Allarmi_Priorita_00_SET, which copies it into Alarm_Head.

steps.title: Search for the flag
text: Search the filling PLC for **Alarm_Head[0].Pos[77]** to find the logic that raises alarm 477.

documents.title: Bosch servo main drives re-zero
documents.summary: Re-home the filler or capper turret on machines with Bosch servo main drives.

meta.Machine: Fillers and cappers with Bosch servo main drive

safety: Work in Maintenance mode with the emergency stop pressed while you turn the turret by hand.

steps.title: Abort the e-cam (capper)
text: On a capper with an electronic cam, abort the e-cam first.

steps.title: Turn the filler to mechanical zero
text: In Maintenance mode press the emergency stop and turn the filler turret by hand until the locator under the machine lines up with its marker.

steps.title: Turn the capper to mechanical zero
text: Do the same for the capper. Its zero marker is on the back of the capping turret, with an indentation in the turret plate to line up with.

steps.title: Home from the HMI
text: Still in Maintenance mode, log in as user 1 on the grey HMI page and open the **Carousel parameters** tab.
With the turret at its zero marker, press the home button for that carousel.

steps.title: Confirm
text: The actual value should change to 0/360. Any other value means the carousel did not home. Repeat the procedure.

documents.title: Servo capper belt tension check
documents.summary: Check the tension of the capping head drive belts on SIRIO servo cappers.
safety: Isolate the machine from electric power before reaching into the capper.

steps.title: Measure with a tension meter
text: Check each capping head drive belt. The resonance frequency should be **160 to 165 Hz**.
steps.caption: Capping head drive belts

steps.title: Or check by hand
text: Press the middle of the belt with a finger. It should move in **less than 3 to 4 mm**.

steps.title: Adjust if needed
text: If the tension is out of range, adjust it as described in the machine manual section on drive belt tension.

steps.title: Check the other belts
text: While isolated, also check the spindle grip inserts for wear, the cap release cylinder for smooth movement, and the power distribution belts for tension and wear.

documents.title: Copying the Bosch image to a CF card
documents.summary: Write a saved Bosch controller image onto the machine CF card with HDD Raw Copy.
safety: Switch the machine off before removing or inserting the CF card.

steps.title: Connect the card
text: Put the machine CF card in a card reader on your PC.

steps.title: Start HDD Raw Copy
text: Run HDD Raw Copy 1.02. Close every other window before the next step.

steps.title: Choose the image
text: Select File, then Image, and press Continue. Select the correct .IMGC file and press Open, then Continue.

steps.title: Choose the CF card
text: Select the CF card (USB reader) as the destination and press Continue.

steps.title: Write the card
text: Press START, then Yes. Wait while it shows Copying, until the Task complete message, then close the program.

steps.title: Fit the card
text: Switch the machine off, insert the programmed CF card and restart.

documents.title: Bosch IndraMotion service tool: log file upload
documents.summary: Save the Bosch drive diagnostic log from the capper so Ronchi and Bosch can find the root cause of a drive fault.

steps.title: Connect to the machine
text: Plug into the ethernet port on the left door of the capper main electrical panel.

steps.title: Set your PC address
text: Give your PC a free address on the machine network. Addresses are on the topology map in the electrical drawings. The network is normally 192.168.10.x or 192.168.11.x, mask 255.255.255.0.

steps.title: Open the service tool
text: In a web browser, type the IP address of the Bosch Rexroth motion logic controller (MLC) from the topology map. It is normally 192.168.10.17, 192.168.11.17, 192.168.10.50 or 192.168.11.50.
The IndraMotion MS/Explorer service tool opens. Log in with the IndraMotion administrator account (Bosch default; ask Ronchi service if you do not have it).

steps.title: Save the diagnostics
text: On the diagnostic overview, click the Save icon. Select all devices, choose .html as the format and press OK.

steps.title: Wait for the upload
text: Extraction takes a few minutes; a progress bar shows at the top. When a new browser window opens, save it as an .html file to the desktop.

steps.title: Send it to Ronchi
text: Email the .html log file to service@ronchiamerica.com.

rows: 800-739-7684, leave a message for a call back

documents.title: Bosch height limit change
documents.summary: Change the minimum or maximum height limit of a Bosch-controlled turret height adjustment in IndraWorks.
safety: A wrong limit can let a turret travel into the bridge or star. Confirm the new limit mechanically before production.
tools: Laptop with IndraWorks and the machine project

steps.title: Open the MLC properties
text: With the project open, right-click the MLC CPU and choose Properties.

steps.title: Check the connection
text: Under Hardware/communication, run a connection test to make sure you are online with the controller.

steps.title: Open the height constants
text: Go to Logic, Application, VAR_Global, HeightAdjust, **_GlobalConstant_HA**.

steps.title: Change the limit
text: The array holds the height limits for each turret, one row per turret as described in the comments. For example, to change the minimum for capper turret A, change **Lmin** in the first row.

steps.title: Download with online change
text: Log in and choose **Login with online change** with **Update boot project** ticked.

documents.title: Bosch log file login
documents.summary: Open the Rexroth IndraDrive web diagnostics to read motor and controller fault codes.

steps.title: Find the controller address
text: Look up the controller IP address in the wiring diagram. The network topology is usually sheet 161 on Ronchi machines.

steps.title: Open it in a browser
text: Type the controller IP address into any web browser.

steps.title: Log in as administrator
text: The page opens as guest. Log in with the IndraMotion administrator account to see the diagnostics. Use the Bosch default credentials, which the Ronchi service lead can give you.

steps.title: Read the faults
text: Use the tree on the left. Each motor and the controller show any active fault or fault code.

documents.title: Bosch servo motor change with homing
documents.summary: Swap a Bosch servo motor, move its address and parameter memory to the new motor, and home it.
safety: Lock out the machine before removing the motor plugs.

steps.title: Remove the plug lock and plugs
text: Remove the plug lock, then the two plugs.

steps.title: Note the address
text: Check and note the motor address switches.

steps.title: Remove the parameter memory
text: Open the plate that covers the memory and remove the memory module. It holds the motor parameters.

steps.title: Prepare the new motor
text: Set the new motor to the same address, and fit the memory module from the old motor. Install the motor and refit the plugs and plug lock.

steps.title: Set up the machine
text: Capper enabled. If machine modes are present, select MAINTENANCE. Reset alarms. Machine in STOP mode.

steps.title: Home the head
text: Enter the head number and press the homing button. The head moves slowly up until it reads the homing sensor and saves its reference.

callouts.label: Spindles
callouts.text: Spindle motors home on the first run. For an orienting chuck, adjust it mechanically after homing. On RSC machines the same homing is on the Layout Motors page.

documents.title: Bosch spindle home adjustment for ball screws
documents.summary: Bring all capper spindle heads to the same height by adjusting each head's home sensor and re-homing it.

meta.Machine: Bosch e-cam cappers with ball screws

safety: Abort the heads before moving the sensor flag. Keep hands clear when homing.
tools: Material to cut a height gauge

steps.title: Flatten the e-cam
text: Set the e-cam Y axis to all 0. All heads then stay at the same height around the capper.

steps.title: Pick a reference head
text: There is no fixed reference height. Choose one head and measure it as the baseline.

steps.title: Make a gauge
text: Cut a gauge to that measurement. Jog each head to the same point on the bridge and check it with the gauge. Within 1 mm is acceptable.

steps.title: Adjust the home flag
text: Abort the heads. Move the sensor flag closer to the sensor to make the spindle lower, or further away to make it higher. Make sure the sensor stays on after the move.
On cappers with the sensor on a rod, loosen the screws marked W and slide the rod and sensor up or down.

steps.title: Re-home the head
text: Press the stethoscope icon at the bottom right of the HMI to open the capper parameters page (log in as user 1). Press the right arrow twice, enter the head number and press **ECAM HOME**. You must home it this way to store the new home position.

steps.title: Home all heads and check
text: Go back to the e-cam page and home all heads. Check the new height, then jog to the next head and repeat.

documents.title: Technical note: STO on Bosch Rexroth drives
documents.summary: How to show, for a safety validation, that capper servos are in Safe Torque Off whenever the doors are open.

blocks.heading: Why this matters
text: Some customers validate the safety of monoblocks with servo cappers. With the doors open, pressing reset restores voltage to the capper servos, so voltage alone cannot prove the capper is safely stopped. Ronchi uses the drives' **Safe Torque Off (STO)** function to prevent motion while voltage is present and the guarding is open. The STO status in the IndraMotion Service Tool is the evidence.

steps.title: Connect
text: Connect a computer to the machine network service socket.

steps.title: Open the IndraMotion Service Tool
text: In a browser, enter the IP address of the Bosch Rexroth MLC and log in with the IndraMotion administrator account.

steps.title: Open the safety diagnosis
text: Open one or more real axes and choose **Drive Integrated Safety Technology Diagnosis**.
steps.caption: Doors closed, safety circuit complete

steps.title: Open the doors
text: Open the doors without pressing reset. STO is active.
steps.caption: Doors open, no reset

steps.title: Press reset with the doors open
text: Press reset. Voltage returns but STO stays active, so no motion can occur.
steps.caption: Doors open, reset pressed

steps.title: Close the doors and reset
text: Close the doors and clear the alarms. STO releases.
steps.caption: Doors closed, safety reset

documents.title: Capper column replacement (no jack screw)
documents.summary: Lift the capper off its fixed column with a forklift, replace the column and rebuild the capper.

meta.Machine: Cappers with fixed column (no jack screw)

safety: The upper capper weighs about 1,750 kg. Use a forklift rated well above that, with straps through the lifting holes, and keep everyone clear while it is raised.
Disconnect every air and electrical connection between the upper and lower capper before lifting.
tools: Forklift, at least 2,000 kg capacity and about 4,200 mm lift height

steps.title: Set the machine to zero
text: Start with the machine assembled and in normal working condition. Turn it to the mechanical 0 point.

steps.title: Remove change parts
text: Remove the transfer change parts and chucks so the machine can be moved electronically.

steps.title: Make room for the forklift
text: Remove the guard and the exit tunnel so the forklift can get in.

steps.title: Remove the anti-rotation shaft
text: On the upper part, remove the anti-rotation shaft. Unscrew the tube and take it off the column.

steps.title: Loosen the joining flange
text: Loosen the flange screws that join the lower and upper capper.

steps.title: Rig the upper capper
text: Remove the upper cover of the fixed column. Pass lifting straps through the holes.

steps.title: Lift off the upper turret
text: Lift with the forklift until the upper turret clears its outer guard. Expect about 2,000 mm of lift from about 2,200 mm, roughly 4,200 mm in total. Check the real heights on your machine.

steps.title: Move it aside
text: Back the forklift away and set the upper capper down safely until it is reassembled.

steps.title: Strip the column
text: Remove the change part supports that could hit the column. Keep the parts that go on the new column (gear wheel, column support, flange support). The column itself is replaced.

steps.title: Free the column
text: Remove the screws that hold the column flange to the base. Follow the Ronchi technician's instructions and drawing GF076618, and do not remove parts that will be reused.

steps.title: Lift the lower capper and change the column
text: With great care, lift the lower capper. The column can then be replaced.

steps.title: Chamfer and fit the new column
text: Machine a 45 degree chamfer on the bottom plate with a manual mill so the new column goes in. Position it, fix the flange to the base and refit the supports and gear wheel.

steps.title: Reassemble
text: Refit everything removed earlier. Reconnect all pneumatic and electrical circuits, and connect the bearing lubrication pipes to the two inlets on the central column.

documents.title: Capper central column alignment
documents.summary: Re-seat the SIRIO capper central column support on the base frame so the turret travels straight from MIN to MAX.
safety: Keep clear of the turret while it moves between MIN and MAX elevation.

steps.title: Check the base frame feet
text: Make sure the leveling feet under the capper base frame are adjusted, especially those under the turret.

callouts.label: Tip
callouts.text: Pull a string diagonally from corner to corner under the frame to see if it sags or bows up.

steps.title: Lower the turret
text: Lower the capper turret to MIN on the HMI Elevation page.

steps.title: Mark the washers
text: Mark the current position of the four flat washers under the four bolts that hold the column support to the frame.
steps.caption: Central support leveling and mounting bolts

steps.title: Loosen the bolts
text: Loosen, but do not remove, the four hex bolts and the four socket head leveling screws on the column support.

steps.title: Let the column settle
text: Raise the turret to MAX, then lower it back to MIN.

steps.title: Set the leveling screws
text: Turn the four leveling screws in by hand until they meet the frame, then a further 1/4 to 1/2 turn with the Allen wrench.

steps.title: Tighten and test
text: Tighten the four hex bolts. Run the turret to MIN and MAX several times to check.

documents.title: Filler main bearing replacement
documents.summary: Lift the upper filler off its center hub and replace the main radial thrust bearing.
safety: Support the main drive gear before removing the retaining ring. Use a forklift rated at 6,000 lb or more.
Lock out the machine and isolate air and product before starting.
tools: Blocks or bottle jacks for the drive gear
Blocks to set the upper filler on

steps.title: Open up the filler
text: Raise the filler to maximum height. Remove the inner and outer lower covers to reach the center.
steps.caption: Lower covers removed

steps.title: Clear forklift access
text: Remove enough bottle lifting plates for forklift access and to clear the lifting cam at the front.
Turn the filler so the flow meter cable connections through the center are easy to reach and no platforms sit under the cam.

steps.title: Remove what is in the way
text: Remove the product supply line and support from the top, the turret guarding on the forklift side, and anything else in the way.

steps.title: Disconnect cables and air
text: Disconnect all flow meter cables, air lines and wires from the plugs on the lower panel. Pull them up to the top of the filler.

steps.title: Support the gear and free the hub
text: Support the main drive gear with blocks or bottle jacks; jacks also help realign the hub later. Remove the retaining ring that holds the gear to the hub, and the two bolts acting as set screws on the side of the gear hub.
steps.caption: Set screws; gear supported

steps.title: Unbolt the upper plate
text: Remove the eight bolts that hold the upper plate to the center shaft hub.

callouts.label: Important
callouts.text: Mark the alignment of the filler plate to the hub so the filler timing is correct on reassembly.

steps.title: Lift off the upper filler
text: Lift by the upper plate (remove some filling valves for fork access) or, better, by the bottom plate (remove some bottle lifting plates). Set it down on blocks.
steps.caption: Lifting by the bottom plate is best

steps.title: Remove the center hub
text: If the hub has tapped lifting holes, fit temporary lifting rings and lift it out, then plug the holes so liquid cannot reach the bearing later. If not, pry the hub and bearing apart.

steps.title: Replace the bearing
text: The main bearing is under the hub. Remove the grease lines and refit them to the new bearing. Check the bushings inside the center column and replace them if needed.
steps.caption: Main radial thrust bearing

steps.title: Reassemble
text: Reassemble in reverse order, with plenty of anti-seize on all parts.
Check for a position key in the radial slots that aligns the head to the hub; mark it and refit it. Turned-down bolts work well as guide pins when lowering the upper filler back on.

documents.title: Filler bearing replacement: planning and sequence
documents.summary: Plan a 40 to 44 head filler main bearing job: equipment the site must supply, the five activities, and the checks before restart.

meta.Skill: Ronchi service team with site maintenance

safety: The 40 to 44 head filler turret weighs about 3,600 kg (7,936 lb). Lift only with rated equipment and a planned lift path.
tools: Forklift rated 9,000 lb or more with a 3-stage mast
Lifting straps rated 9,000 lb or more: two 4 ft and two 6 ft

blocks.heading: Before Ronchi arrives
bullets: Move everything around the machine that can be moved.
Leave room for the forklift to maneuver before and after it lifts the turret.
Have the forklift, straps and pallets on site.

rows: Check parts received. Back up recipes and the main PLC program. Set the elevation, turn to mechanical home (head 1), lock out power and air. Remove turret Lexan covers and splash guards, base frame covers and anything blocking the base.

Disconnect the supply line and pipes, valve and flow meter wiring. Feed cables down to the base. Support the filler gear on jacks, unbolt the turret from the gear, rig it by the center beams, lift it out onto four pallets. Unbolt the bearing, fit two 16 mm eyebolts and lift it out. Clean the area.

Lift the new bearing in, align its grease point with the grease tube, set and bolt it to the hub. Lift the turret back, align it to the bearing bolt holes, bolt it, bolt the gear back from below, remove the jacks. Re-run and terminate all cables including height limit sensors. Refit guards, pipes and the supply line.
Point-test I/O on the main PLC, remote I/O and filler PLC. Check HMI data and recipes. Test sequences and run single and multiple bottle tests.

blocks.heading: Visual inspection before power-up
bullets: Lower assembly: AC and DC power wiring, ethernet and remote I/O wiring.
Upper assembly: flow meters and valves fitted, cables routed and secured, elevation motor and height limit sensors.
Terminations: flow meters, valves, elevation motor, height limit sensors.
Head 1 sensor and zero degree pointer in the right place.

blocks.heading: Activation checks
bullets: Remove lockout devices, apply AC power and facility air.
Measure AC at the main cabinet and DC at the power supply outputs. Check DC indication on the X500 box and on the HMI.
Confirm communications to the main PLC, filler PLC, HMI and remote I/O.

blocks.heading: Test sequence
bullets: E-stop, guard door safety, motor start and main motor start sequences.
Product delivery and ancillary system sequences.
Single bottle, then multiple bottles: presence detection, tracking, fill detection and reject.

documents.title: Main bearing removal on newer fillers
documents.summary: Replace the main bearing on newer EXACTA fillers, including machines with a static wash ring.
safety: Power down, lock out and shut off the main air before removing anything.
Support the main drive gear before removing the center column bolts. Use a forklift rated 12,000 lb or more with long forks.
tools: Blocks or jacks for the drive gear

steps.title: Open up the filler
text: Raise the filler to maximum height. Remove the upper plastic and lower metal covers.

steps.title: Clear forklift access
text: Remove enough bottle lifting plates for the forklift and to clear the lifting cam.

steps.title: Mark zero
text: Turn the filler to zero and make a clear mark so the timing can be restored on reassembly. Open all doors you will need, then power down and lock out.

steps.title: Disconnect the top of the filler
text: Remove the product supply pipe and anti-rotation arms. Disconnect the pressure transducer, air bleed line and the two air lines.

steps.title: Remove the rear wall
text: Disconnect the door switches and pull their wires from the rear wire way. Remove the rear wall bolts, including those on the table top, and take the wall off.

steps.title: Disconnect motors and cables
text: From the top, disconnect the elevation motor and the static wash ring motor, the meter cable plugs and any other cables from the center column.

steps.title: Disconnect the drain
text: Remove the tri-clamp between the drain pipe and the wash ring.

steps.title: Support the drive gear
text: Block or jack the main drive gear in place.

steps.title: Unbolt the column and turret
text: From under the machine remove the six center column bolts. Remove all bolts between the turret plate and the center column hub.

steps.title: Lift off the turret
text: Lift by the upper plate (remove some valves) or, better, by the bottom plate (remove some lifting plates). Set it on blocks.
steps.caption: Lifting by the bottom plate is best

steps.title: Remove the hub
text: Remove all hub bolts, including the 16 underneath. Some are easier to reach from the top through the center. Lift out the hub.

steps.title: Change the bearing
text: Remove the grease lines and the bolts around the bearing, lift it out and fit the new one. Refit the grease lines. Check the center column bushings.

callouts.label: Before running
callouts.text: Grease the new bearing.

steps.title: Reassemble
text: Reassemble in reverse order with plenty of anti-seize. Line up the hub and turret with your marks. Reconnect every wire and refit all covers, lifting platforms and anything else removed.

documents.title: Batching meter configuration in Studio 5000

blocks.heading: Symptom

steps.title: Find the rung
text: In Studio 5000 go to Task 01, **EM40_Filler**, **CM80_Filler_FlowCmd**, rung 20.

steps.title: Set the meter type
text: Change the constant **KfilTubeDiamA** through Monitor Tags to match the meter fitted.
The output **HMIFillerA.FlowMng.Write.RT_FlowType** feeds R_AOI_FillingMain: latched = 1 = mass, unlatched = 0 = mag.

steps.title: Initialize the meter

documents.title: Updating Dosimass flowmeter firmware
documents.summary: Update DOSIMASS flowmeters from firmware 3.00.07 to 3.00.08 with the E+H modem, RCScripter and Remote Control.
tools: Flowmeter update folder (on the PC desktop)
E+H FXA291 service modem (Ronchi America has one)

steps.title: Prepare the PC
text: Copy the flowmeter update folder to the desktop and install Remote Control 2018.
Connect the FXA291 modem and note which COM port it uses.

steps.title: Connect to the meter
text: USB to the PC, the orange right-angle connector to the meter, and the large black connector to the meter cable from the filling PLC box.

steps.title: Open RCScripter
text: Run RCScripter.exe from the RCScripter folder. Right-click the bottom banner to set baud rate to Auto and the COM port to the modem's port.

steps.title: Connect
text: Connect to the meter. The green light comes on and the current firmware shows.

steps.title: Run the patch
text: Close RCScripter and double-click **Patch_Dosimass.BAT**. A window opens while it runs and closes when done.

steps.title: Connect with Remote Control
text: Open Remote Control. Set baud Auto, the COM port, and select **CDI** under Select Interface. Connect and check the light is on.

steps.title: Check the patch
text: Check the parameter changed by the BAT file to confirm the patch took.

steps.title: Flash the firmware
text: Choose **Flash** and select the file **71312108_201806191138_Dosimass_MOD_FLCO_App_30008.XML**.

steps.title: Confirm the version
text: Let the page reload and check the new version before moving to the next meter.

blocks.heading: Notes
bullets: Next meters connect automatically with the same settings.
The meters do not need re-parameterizing. The programming cable is only for new meters.
Record each meter's serial number and send the list to Ronchi Italy.
Reconnect each flowmeter cable to the right meter after its update.

steps.title: Drain the meter

steps.caption: Meter with shut-off valve

steps.title: Lock out
text: Stop the machine and lock out.

steps.title: Disconnect the cables
text: Remove the cables from the top and bottom of the meter: B, meter to PLC communication; C, meter to MAC valve command; D, ground.
steps.caption: Cables B, C and D

steps.title: Remove the meter
text: Loosen and remove the tri-clamps. Remove the meter and write down its head number.

steps.title: Fit the new meter
text: Clean the flanges, fit new gaskets and install the new meter with the old tri-clamps. The flow arrow on the label must point down toward the MAC valve.
steps.caption: Flow direction arrow points down

steps.title: Reconnect ground and valve only
text: Open the shut-off valve if fitted. Connect ground D and MAC valve cable C. Do **not** connect the PLC cable B yet.

steps.title: Connect the programming cable
text: Connect the WMBPROG cable from the meter's top connector (8-pin M12 male) to communication port **-XP309.1** (4-pin M12 female) in box **-X501** inside the turret. The port may be inside or outside the box.
steps.caption: Box -X501 in the filler turret

steps.title: Open the flowmeter maintenance page
text: On the HMI press Diagnostics (level 2 password), then the arrow to **Filler Flowmeters Maintenance** (level 1 password).

steps.title: Re-initialize

steps.caption: Download complete

steps.title: Write the head number
text: Enter the head number you noted and press **Write** (G).

steps.title: Reconnect for production

steps.title: Check communication
text: Press **Show Comm Status** (F). With good communication, requests sent equal responses received. If there are errors, press Re-initialize again.

callouts.label: If it fails
callouts.text: A red banner reads COMMUNICATION ERROR. Check the maintenance cable, press Re-initialize, then Verify (J) on the In-depth Parameters page (button H). Red X marks show parameters that do not match the default.

blocks.heading: Calibrate only when
bullets: The product is good and free of air.
Delivery pressure is steady within plus or minus 0.2 bar of the preset.
Temperature and viscosity are at normal operating conditions.
All nozzles, restrictors and screens are clean and the same size. Check the Filling Area bar graph that all heads fill at about the same rate.
Calibrate all heads for a new product, a big volume change, a new delivery pressure, or a nozzle, screen or restrictor change.

callouts.label: Samples
callouts.text: Only use bottles rejected by Quality Control while the machine runs continuously. Do not use bottles rejected for any other reason. Ignore any one sample that is far off, and do not weigh samples taken while the machine stopped.

steps.title: Tare the scale
text: Zero the QA scale with an empty bottle and cap.

steps.title: Open Quality Control
text: On the Quality Control Filler / On Line Production / Statistics screen, press the down arrow under the Quality Control column.
steps.caption: Quality Control screen

steps.title: Run the QC
text: With the filler running normally, enter First head (F7), Last head (F8) and Repetitions (1). Press F6 START. Collect the rejected bottles in order, weigh them and list the weights by head number.
Repeat at least three times.

steps.title: Open Flowmeter Calibration
text: Press the up arrow, then the right arrow to Filling Preset / Machine Speed / Product Pressure. Press the down arrow under Filling Preset. Press the Cal icon (bottle and scale), then the Keys icon and log in at level 1.

steps.title: Enter the head and weight
text: Start with the first head rejected. Press F2 Calibrating Head and enter the head number. Press F3 Sample Weight and enter that head's average weight.
steps.caption: Flowmeter Calibration screen

steps.title: Calculate
text: Press **Calibrate on QC** for a new product or **Calibrate on Average** for an established product. Compare the new and previous results.

steps.title: Accept or abort
text: If the values look right, press **Accept Calibration** and move to the next head. If not, press Abort and re-enter the values.

steps.title: Save to the recipe
text: Press the left arrow to Recipe / Washing Control / Height Adjustment, then the down arrow to the Recipe List. Save the calibration values to the recipe for each product and dose.

blocks.heading: Calibrate on average
text: During normal running the filler keeps the last 12 fill values for each head and averages them. Run a Quality Control and compare weights. For heads out of range, calibrate as above using **Calibrate on Average**.

callouts.label: Good practice
callouts.text: Only calibrate a head that is outside the fill limits, and check at least three samples first. If calibration or correction values look odd, reset the base count and correction values to the factory settings and start again. For a new product, contact Ronchi America to test the best nozzle, screen, speed and restrictor set-up.

documents.title: Bosch capper encoder alignment
documents.summary: Set the monoblock electrical zero and synchronize the Rexroth e-cam capper turret to it.
safety: Remove all bottles first. Jog in Manual mode only.

steps.title: Clear and set up
text: Remove all bottles and put the machine in Manual mode.

steps.title: Align the filler to mechanical zero
text: Jog the filler until zero pointer A lines up with zero mark B on the turret lower disk C.
steps.caption: Pointer A, mark B, disk C

steps.title: Check head 1 and the bottle sensor
text: Filling nozzle 1 (I) should be in the first filling position, with its bottle platform (L) up at the exit of the platform cam.
The bottle detection sensor beam (M) should hit the center of the bottle pocket (N).

steps.title: Read the machine position
text: Open the Diagnostics screen and read Machine Position (E). If it is not 0 plus or minus 5 degrees, adjust the encoder.

steps.title: Adjust the machine encoder
text: The encoder (F) is low on the driveline, usually on the infeed scroll drive column. Loosen its lock collar (G), turn the encoder until Machine Position reads 0 plus or minus 5 degrees, and lock the collar while holding that value.
Encoder models and collars vary, but the method is the same.

steps.title: Power cycle
text: With the main electrical zero set, switch off the feed to the main electrical cabinet. Wait 30 seconds and switch it back on.

steps.title: Home the servos
text: After boot-up the servos must home and synchronize to the machine encoder. Start the capper turret turning, in automatic or manual. When it passes mechanical zero, synchronization completes and the homing indication goes off.

steps.title: Check the positions
text: Stop the capper turret at mechanical zero. Machine position should read 0 (0 to +5 degrees) and Capper Position 0 (0 to +2 degrees). If both are in tolerance the procedure is complete.

steps.title: Align the filler to mechanical zero
text: Jog the filler until zero pointer A lines up with zero mark B on the turret lower disk C.

text: Filling nozzle 1 (I) should be in the first filling position, with its bottle platform (L) up at the exit of the platform cam.

steps.title: Read the machine position
text: Open the Diagnostics screen and read Machine Position (E). If it is not 0 plus or minus 5 degrees, adjust the encoder.

steps.title: Adjust the machine encoder
text: The encoder (F) is low on the driveline, usually on the infeed scroll drive column. Loosen its lock collar (G), turn the encoder until Machine Position reads 0 plus or minus 5 degrees, and lock the collar while holding that value.

steps.title: Align the capper to mechanical zero
text: With the main electrical zero set and the machine in Manual, jog until the capper zero pointer A lines up with mark B on the capper lower disk C.

steps.title: Read the capper position
text: On the Diagnostics screen, Capper Position (E) should read 0 plus or minus 2 degrees. If not, adjust the capper encoder.

text: The capper encoder is on top of the capper turret. Loosen set screw F on the linkage between the encoder shaft and the drive gear shaft. Turn the linkage until Capper Position reads 0 plus or minus 2 degrees and tighten the set screw while holding it.

steps.title: Verify
text: Turn the capper one full revolution and stop at mechanical zero. Machine Position should be 0 plus or minus 5 degrees and Capper Position 0 plus or minus 2 degrees. If not, repeat the alignment.

blocks.heading: What was tested
text: Ronchi America's fill test lab estimated the current spring rates and tested three stiffer Lee Spring parts: LC095J03M (music wire), LC095J03S (stainless) and LHL750A02. LC095J03M was chosen.

steps.title: Log in to SQL Server
text: From WW_CLNT open SQL Server Management Studio. Server name: the industrial PC name or IP. Authentication: SQL Server, with the Ronchi SQL account (from the service lead).

steps.title: Start the backup
text: Expand the server, then Databases. Databases are always prefixed RN_, for example RN_4092MB. Right-click it, Tasks, Back Up.

steps.title: Set the destination
text: Remove every existing destination path, then Add, File Name. Choose the location and name the file exactly as the database plus .bak. Make sure no file of that name already exists. The path is on the industrial PC, not the VM.

steps.title: Overwrite and run
text: On Media Options choose **Overwrite all existing backup sets**, click OK and wait for the completed message.

steps.title: Connect to the industrial PC
text: From WW_CLNT, connect by VNC to the industrial PC and close the SCADA runtime for the backup.

steps.title: Back up the GLX
text: Open System Platform Management Console, Galaxy Database Manager. Right-click the galaxy, Backup, Yes. Save it next to the database backup and keep the suggested name (GLX_<order>MB.cab).

steps.title: Copy the files off
text: From WW_CLNT, open the industrial PC's C$ share in Windows Explorer and copy both backups to the Ronchi server. Restart the SCADA runtime if you closed it.

steps.title: Use a physical PC
text: Recipes must be exported from a physical PC (not a VM) with Excel and Power Query, connected to the machine network.

steps.title: Run the recipe workbook
text: Copy the recipe template for the machine type (monoblock, Betel or batch) from the master documents folder, enter the machine details and refresh the data. See also the guide Saving RSC recipe data.

steps.title: Restore the database
text: In SQL Server Management Studio right-click Databases, Restore Database, Device, Add, and pick the .bak. Rename the target to RN_<order> and, only if overwriting, tick the overwrite options. Wait for Restore successful.

steps.title: Restore the galaxy
text: Turn the runtime off; a galaxy restore can only be done locally on the PC or VM. In System Platform Management Console, Galaxy Database Manager, right-click the galaxy (same name), Restore, Yes, and pick the .cab.

steps.title: Clean up and deploy
text: Still in the console, right-click Platform Manager and choose **Remove Local Platform** to clear the old run folders. Then open the IDE and deploy the whole application; after a restore it is undeployed.

tools: Small screwdriver for zero and span

steps.title: Set the analog channel
text: Channel 0 must be scaled 2 to 60 psig.

steps.title: Disable the old logic
text: In **QT1_PV_60_S-LD16_TankPressure**, add AFI to rungs 20, 21 and 23.

steps.title: Add the Nitra logic
text: Add the new rungs for the Nitra controller below them.

steps.title: Set span at maximum
text: Set the tank pressure set point to maximum. Turn the Nitra **span** until the tank reaches the set point.

steps.title: Set zero

blocks.heading: Why
text: Some plants want the outfeed belt to stop while the machine is suspended for an outfeed condition (outfeed full, downstream pause), and restart with machine rotation when it clears. The outfeed belt Add-On Instruction needs a small change.

steps.title: Use the suspended flag
text: On the outfeed belt conveyor AOI call, use **PackML.suspended** for **Standby_Mode_Flag**. This can be done online.

documents.title: Capper spindle brake replacement (ELAU)
documents.summary: Remove two spindle assemblies to reach the servo brake, replace the brake, and fit the dump and check valves.
safety: Lock out the machine and bleed off the air before disconnecting cables and air lines.
Stand on a step stool inside the capper enclosure only with the turret locked out.
tools: Air supply above 3 bar for testing

blocks.heading: Remove two spindle assemblies
text: Removing the two spindles next to the brake gives easy access to the brake and its bracket.

steps.title: Position the capper
text: Turn the capper so you can put a step stool inside the enclosure. Pick two spindle units side by side.

steps.title: Remove the chuck
text: Remove the chuck from each spindle you are taking out.

steps.title: Disconnect the spindle
text: Disconnect the three sensor cables, the two I/O cables on the lower servo, the green combination cable and ground on each servo, and the grip cylinder air lines. Remove the lower belt and the large pulley.

steps.title: Unbolt the spindle
text: Remove the four Allen bolts under the spindle and the two on the middle support plate. Remove the upper L bracket and disconnect the brake air line.

steps.title: Lift it out
text: Lift the spindle out through the cut-out in the lower disk. Repeat for the second spindle.

steps.title: Remove the brake bracket
text: Remove the two Allen bolts that hold the brake L bracket to the spindle assembly, and the two lock nuts that hold the brake to the bracket (keep them).

callouts.label: Spacing
callouts.text: Four spring washers, two per bolt, set the gap between brake and bracket. Note their orientation and the gap.

steps.title: Swap the brake
text: Remove the two bolts holding the brake to the bracket and fit the new brake the same way round, with the same gap and washers.

steps.title: Check for drag
text: Refit the brake assembly. Connect air directly to the brake: it needs more than 3 bar to open. Check it does not drag on the disk. Repeat for each brake.

steps.title: Refit the spindles
text: Reinstall the spindle assemblies in reverse order.

blocks.heading: Fit the dump and check valves

steps.title: Dump valve
text: Fit the supplied dump valve in the air feed at the top of the slip ring, in the line that feeds the brakes.

steps.title: Check valve
text: Fit the check valve in the pressure manifold for the tube grippers, after the T fitting from the slip ring.

steps.title: Home and test
text: Run the first phase of the capper homing sequence. Open a door to remove air from the brakes and check the spindle shafts do not move while braked. Check the tube grippers keep their air pressure.

documents.title: eWON Cosy 131 quick reference
