Ronchi America eCatcher account (from the service lead)

blocks.heading: Know the box
bullets: Runs on 12 to 24 V DC. Boot takes about 25 seconds; then only PWR stays steady green and USR blinks green slowly.
USR blinking red (one short, one long) means boot was interrupted, most often by a duplicate IP address.
Port 1 is always LAN and is used for updates and recovery. Port 4 is WAN by default.
It is a remote access VPN router, not a switch.
Its LAN range must differ from both the company LAN and the site LAN.
eWON technical support: +1 888-826-9287.
blocks.caption: Front panel

steps.title: Log in to eCatcher
text: Open eCatcher and log in with the Ronchi America account.

steps.title: Add the eWON
text: Click Add, enter the eWON name and description and choose a Permanent connection.

steps.title: Copy the key
text: On the Talk2M connectivity page, Copy to Clipboard.

steps.title: Cable it
text: PC to port 1. Company network switch to port 4.

steps.title: Set its IP with eBuddy
text: In eBuddy click Set IP, enter the eWON serial number (with dashes) and the IP address you chose. It then appears in the Maintenance Utility list.

steps.title: Open the wizard
text: Click Open Browser in eBuddy, then the Settings tab. The username is always adm; a new unit uses the default password, which you should change.

steps.title: LAN and WAN
text: Port 4 is WAN (internet). Port 1 is LAN and cannot be changed.

steps.title: Internet
text: Leave Initialize Configuration unticked. Choose Digital Input not used (firmware 11) or Ethernet INTERNET connection (firmware 13). Choose DHCP for the WAN. Leave proxy unticked unless the site uses one.

steps.title: Talk2M
text: Paste the activation key, click Next, leave HTTP proxy unticked and click Next to test the Talk2M connection.

steps.title: Connect
text: In eCatcher select the eWON and click Connect.

blocks.heading: Add a device on the machine network
text: In eCatcher select the eWON, click Properties, then Add LAN Device and enter the device name and IP address.

rows: Disconnect from eCatcher and change it in eBuddy, or in eCatcher: Properties, LAN and Firewall, Modify LAN Subnet.
The eWON range overlaps a device on the LAN. Change the eWON range.
The company firewall may block it. Update the firmware and ask the site IT team to allow the Cosy.
VPN blocked by the external key switch
Check the Line Communications button on the HMI is pressed.
Check the WAN and LAN cables and ports.

documents.title: Betel robot fine calibration (Codian delta robot)
documents.summary: Fine-calibrate the five axes of a Betel unscrambler delta robot with the calibration templates and the ABB FlexPendant.

meta.Machine: Betel unscramblers with Codian/ABB delta robots

safety: The machine must be in Manual and stopped. When you hold the brake release button the axis can drop: support the arm by hand.
Calibration overwrites stored positions and cannot be undone. Only calibrate the axes you have set on the template.
tools: Axis templates (1 to 3, and 4/5 flange template)
Keyboard or FlexPendant for the robot

steps.title: Fit the bracket
text: Fit the blue bracket on the robot's upper plate, next to the axis you are calibrating, and tighten it so there is no play at all.

steps.title: Unhook the arms
text: Unhook the arms from the motor of the axis being calibrated.

steps.title: Release the brake and set the axis
text: Press and hold the black brake release button, usually near the bottle vision belt. Move the axis until the ball sits under the calibration template, then release the button.

steps.title: Open fine calibration
text: On the FlexPendant: menu, Calibration, ROB_1, Calib. Parameters, **Fine Calibration**. Accept the warning about placing the robot on external equipment.

steps.title: Update robot memory if asked
text: If the controller or robot was exchanged, first open Robot Memory, Update, and confirm loading robot data from the controller. This overwrites robot memory and cannot be undone.

steps.title: Calibrate the axis
text: Tick only the axis on the template (for example rob1_1), tap Calibrate, confirm, and wait for **Fine calibration finished successfully**.

steps.title: Repeat for axes 2 and 3
text: Move the bracket and template to axis 2, set it and calibrate rob1_2. Do the same for axis 3. Re-hook the arms.

steps.title: Set approximate positions
text: Holding the brake release, move axis 4 to about 0 degrees and axis 5 to about 90 degrees.

steps.title: Fit the flange template
text: Position and screw on the calibration template.

steps.title: Match the flange
text: Release the brake and move axes 4 and 5 by hand until the flange matches the template sideways and vertically.

steps.title: Calibrate 4 and 5
text: In Fine Calibration tick rob1_4 and rob1_5, Calibrate, confirm, OK. Remove the template.

documents.title: Betel: new recipe on a puck line
documents.summary: Create a new bottle format on a Betel puck line: PLC recipe, PickMaster project and bottle model, PLC to PickMaster link, and pick and place tuning.
tools: Sample bottles (one with a hole drilled at the pick height)

blocks.heading: Main steps
bullets: Make and save the new PLC recipe.
Copy an existing, tested PickMaster project and set the bottle size.
Train the bottle model for each camera.
Configure the PLC to PickMaster link (RIS).

steps.title: Enter and save the recipe
text: Enter all recipe values on the HMI main page. On the recipe page, Read from PLC, then enter the new recipe name, recipe number and a **PickMaster ID** different from every other recipe. Save.

steps.title: Copy a tested project
text: On the PickMaster PC, open a tested project from the ABB Projects folder and Save As the new format.

steps.title: Set the bottle size
text: Set the bottle size on the place and pick items, and apply the pick item to all robots.

steps.title: Open the model
text: Double-click Position Source Configuration (yellow square), then Model.

steps.title: Grab an image
text: Drill a hole in the middle of a bottle at the pick height. Put it on the vision belt over the back light for the first camera and press Live. Check alignment on the grid and that the hole is visible, then save the image so you can reuse it.

steps.title: Define and train
text: Click Define. Fit the green area to the bottle edge and center the yellow point on the hole. Click Train and tick Show model to check it.

steps.title: Repeat for each camera
text: Repeat the image, define and train steps for every camera.

steps.title: Open RIS configuration
text: In the project click RIS Configuration, then Configure.

steps.title: Set the project commands
text: First number = the PickMaster ID in the PLC recipe. Second = 0. Third = 1 to 5 for the commands. Set every robot as in the table.

blocks.heading: Tuning pick and place
text: Before changing anything, film the problem in slow motion. Start a new format at low machine speed. Change values in small steps. On some machines these settings are also on the HMI.

rows: Robot presses too hard on the bottle
Pick work area, Tune: raise Z, up to 5 mm at a time
Pick work area, Tune: lower Z, up to 5 mm at a time
Bottle not centered in the gripper
Place work area, Tune: raise X, up to 5 mm at a time
Bottle released before both grippers close
Place conveyor work area: reduce vacuum reversion, 0.01 s at a time
Bottle stays stuck on the cups
Place conveyor work area: increase vacuum reversion, 0.01 s at a time
General instability on a new format
Raise Z place, lower robot speed (robot settings), slow the machine and vision belt

documents.title: Betel belt tensioning, bearing and shaft assembly
documents.summary: Tension Betel conveyor belts to a standard 0.7% stretch, and lock roller bearing grub screws so they cannot work loose.
safety: Lock out the conveyor before tensioning or working on rollers.

blocks.heading: Belt tensioning
text: Belt makers quote working load at 1% stretch (N/mm). Stretch applied at assembly ranges from 0.4% for light loads to 1.2% for heavy loads. More than that is not recommended because of the belt's elastic memory. Ronchi standardizes on **0.7%**.

steps.title: Mark 1000 mm
text: With the belt slack, mark exactly 1000 mm along its edge.

steps.title: Tension to 1007 mm
text: Tension the belt until the marks are 1007 mm apart.

steps.title: Run and re-measure
text: Run the belt a few turns so the tension spreads along its length, then take the final measurement and adjust.
steps.caption: Marking, tensioning and checking 1000 to 1007 mm

steps.title: Remove the grub screws
text: With the roller positioned and centered in the frame, temporarily remove the two bearing grub screws.

steps.title: Drill the seats
text: With a 5 mm drill, make a 2.5 mm deep seat in the roller shaft for each grub screw tip.

steps.title: Refit with Loctite
text: Refit the grub screws with Loctite so their tips sit in the new seats.

documents.title: Cognex camera guide
documents.summary: Use the Cognex In-Sight software on the operator panel: select and match camera jobs, log in, edit tools, save and load jobs, and what each tool setting means.

meta.Skill: Operator and technician (users 1 and 2 to edit)

steps.title: Find the camera button
text: Camera buttons are usually on the capper page. Look for the camera symbol.
steps.caption: Capper page

steps.title: Job selection page
text: Each camera has its own job selection page with **Trigger Point** (where the camera takes its image), **Machine Position** (current position of head 1) and the list of camera jobs. When the machine position reaches the trigger point, the camera fires.

blocks.heading: Camera jobs must match
text: Jobs are stored only in the camera's own memory, not anywhere else on the machine. Job names in the camera start with a number, and that number must match the position of the job in the blue list on the HMI. For example, camera job 1-Oval Cap 118ml must be selected as the first job in the blue list. Adding a job to the camera means adding its name to the HMI list too.

callouts.label: Mismatch
callouts.text: If the HMI selection and the job loaded in the camera do not match, the camera goes offline until they do.

steps.title: Open the Image Window
text: Press the black and yellow In-Sight button at the bottom of the job selection page. In the Image Window you can watch production, view past images in the filmstrip, and (users 1 and 2) take the camera online or offline, edit tools and change settings. Camera logins are the same as the machine's unless changed on request.

steps.title: Log in
text: Press the gear (settings) icon, then Log On at the top left, and enter your credentials. Back in the Image Window you now have Parameters, Online/Offline and a manual trigger. The trigger only works offline.

steps.title: Edit tools
text: Press Parameters. Tools depend on the application, so not every job has the same ones. Save the job when you are happy.

blocks.heading: What the tools and settings mean

rows: Finds the cap by the contrast between cap and background in its box. Every other tool is positioned from it.
Which transition the tool looks for, light to dark or dark to light, in the direction of the arrows on its box. Wrong polarity makes the tool fail.
Count of dark or light pixels in the tool, shown as the Last score. Set pass and fail limits on it.
A Model Region around a feature that differs front to back (for example the ribbon on a dome flip cap), searched for inside a larger Find Region.
How long the shutter stays open. Higher is brighter.
Brightness and background detail. Higher is brighter with more detail and noise.
Finds the cap's top edge and draws a line; compared with the Misplace Line.
If the top edge line is above it, the cap is too high and fails.
Processing time. Fewer and smaller tools run faster; keep search regions only as big as needed.

blocks.caption: Model region (red) inside the search region (blue)

steps.title: Save
text: Open camera settings, log on (users 1 and 2), take the camera offline, return to settings, save the job, then log off and put the camera back online.

steps.title: Load it in the camera
text: Open camera settings, log on, take the camera offline, return to settings and open the job. Note its position number. Log off and put the camera online.

steps.title: Match it on the HMI
text: On the blue job selection page select the job at the same position, then save the machine recipe.

documents.title: Teaching the Cognex camera cap colors
documents.summary: Open In-Sight from the HMI, log in, trigger an image at the right machine position and teach the cap color.

meta.Machine: PackML machines with Cognex cap color check

steps.title: Go to the capper
text: From the machine layout page select the capping turret graphic, then **Capper Setup 2**.

steps.title: Open the software
text: Select the Tool icon, then the In-Sight icon. You must be logged in at level 1 or 2 to see it.

steps.title: Log on
text: System Parameters and Reset Counters are grey until you log in. Select the gear icon, then Log On at the top left, and enter the level 1 login. Select Done.

steps.title: Take the camera offline
text: The buttons turn green and you can take the camera offline. Offline lets you trigger it by hand, which you need to teach a color.

steps.title: Jog to the trigger position
text: From Capper Parameters select the camcorder icon. Jog the machine until Machine Position matches **Cam 04**, within about 5 degrees. The bottle is then in the right place.

steps.title: Trigger an image
text: Press the trigger button.

steps.title: Teach
text: Select System Parameters, then **Teach Color**. The hue, saturation and intensity actual values drop to zero, showing the new color is taught. Put the camera back online.

documents.title: Adding or replacing a Cognex camera
documents.summary: Give a new Cognex camera its network address and name, then restore the saved job and settings to it.
tools: Laptop with In-Sight Explorer on the machine network
Camera backup folder (named after the camera)

steps.title: Find the new camera
text: In In-Sight Explorer choose System, Add Sensor/Device to Network. New cameras show with a MAC address but no IP address.

steps.title: Set address and name
text: Select the camera, choose Use the following network settings, and enter the IP address, subnet mask and the correct camera name. Click Apply; the camera restarts and appears in the In-Sight network.

steps.title: Restore the backup
text: System, Restore From. Select the camera and the backup folder with the same name as the camera.

documents.title: Creating a new tool in a Cognex job
documents.summary: Add a new inspection tool to an In-Sight spreadsheet job, expose it on the HMI parameters page, and send its pass or fail to the PLC.
safety: Make all changes with the camera offline, and save a copy of the job before you start.
tools: In-Sight Explorer online to the camera (or the offline emulator)

steps.title: Open the job
text: Open the .job to change. For a new job, copy a similar existing job.

steps.title: Make room in the parameters view
text: Right-click the Parameters button and choose Edit Function to add cells to the custom view.

steps.title: Copy an existing control row
text: Click Parameters, copy an existing function row (for example Presence with its edges, polarity, value, threshold and intensity) and paste it. Right-click, Edit Function to rename it (for example New Region). Add or remove a fixture reference as needed. Note the cells it uses.

steps.title: Make a logic area
text: In the spreadsheet, below the existing tools, make an area for the new logic. Copy an existing set of Get row, column, high, wide, angle and curve cells into it and link them to the new parameters control by editing each Get cell.

steps.title: Add a Plot Region
text: Add a Plot Region tool (copy one, or View, Palette) so the region can be adjusted from the HMI. Point its row, column, high, wide and so on at the new cells.

steps.title: Add the measuring tool
text: The plot only draws. Add the tool that measures: histogram, find segment, find line, extract blobs and so on. Give it the same region cells as the plot.

steps.title: Add ErrFree and String cells
text: Wrap the result you will judge on (threshold, contrast, dark count, bright count...) in an ErrFree, then a String cell so the value shows as a number, including zero, on the parameters page and the status light. Make the formula cells match your new cells.

steps.title: Compare with an If
text: Add an If that compares the measured value with the threshold from the parameters page. 0 is fail, 1 is pass. Choose less than or greater than as the application needs.

steps.title: Color the region and the light
text: Set the plot region color from the If cell (+7 for green), and point the status light at the If cell.

blocks.heading: Send the result to the PLC

steps.title: Copy a write function
text: Copy an existing PLC write function, rename it for the new tool and point it at the new If cell.

steps.title: Add it to the buffer
text: Double-click the buffer tool, select the last output and click Add. Select the new result cell and set the data type to bit instead of 32-bit float.

steps.title: Save and test
text: Save the job, put the camera online and test with good and bad samples. Check the PLC rejects on a fail.

documents.title: Checking the Cognex result equation
documents.summary: Check that every inspection, such as the misplace line, is included in a Cognex job's final pass or fail result, and add it if not.

meta.Machine: Machines with Cognex cap or pump inspection

safety: Edit with the camera offline and save a backup of the job first.

blocks.heading: Why
text: If an inspection result is missing from the final result equation, that inspection can fail without the bottle being rejected. This was found on a job where misplaced pumps were not rejected.

steps.title: Open the spreadsheet
text: In In-Sight click the Custom View button to switch to the spreadsheet where the tools are built.

steps.title: Read the final result
text: Scroll to the final result cell (B128 in the reference job) and click it once; the equation shows at the top.

steps.title: Read the misplace line result
text: Click the misplace line result cell (B109). It returns 1 (pass) if the top line position (B115) is less than the misplace line position (B90), otherwise 0 (fail). Cell numbers can differ between jobs.

steps.title: Check it is included
text: Look for the misplace line cell inside the final result equation. If it is missing, the misplace check never rejects.

steps.title: Add it
text: Click between the last two parentheses of the final equation, type a comma and the misplace result cell (for example B109). Save the job and test with a misplaced sample.

documents.title: Cognex camera tool adjustments

meta.Machine: Machines with Cognex cap or pump inspection

blocks.heading: Logins

rows: Finds the cap. You should not need to adjust it.
Looks for the domed pattern of the cap.
Looks for the high contrast of the pump cap.
Background detail; too much can cause problems.

blocks.heading: Save a recipe on the HMI

steps.title: Select the recipe
text: On the main RECIPE screen press the down arrow at Recipe Management. Scroll to the recipe, press Select, then OK.

steps.title: Upload the machine values
text: Press the right arrow (lower right) for the management screen. Press the key icon and enter the four-digit machine serial number. Press F6 Upload and watch the values change to the current machine values.

steps.title: Save
text: Press the floppy icon. To make a new recipe instead, touch the New Recipe field, enter a name of up to 8 letters or numbers and press OK, then select it and confirm the overwrite.

steps.title: Connect a keyboard
text: Remove the two cover screws to reach the keyboard pigtail and the floppy door key. Unplug the orange HMI power lead. Plug in the pigtail and keyboard (or straight to the keyboard socket on the back). If there is no floppy drive, plug one into the FDD connector now. Reconnect power and close the cover.

steps.title: Exit to Application Manager
text: After boot, go to a main screen (F2 or a down arrow). Press the key icon and enter the service code. Press the gear icon (or the exit function key on older versions), then Go to A.M. and Accept. The screen shows C:\interact\am.

steps.title: Check the files
text: Type cd C:\interact\recipe, then dir.

steps.title: Copy
text: Insert a floppy. Make a recipe folder on it (md A:\recipe), then xcopy C:\interact\recipe\*.* A:\recipe. Type dir A:\recipe to check.

steps.title: Find the application folder
text: Type cd C:\interact\appfile, then dir to find the machine's application folder, and cd into it.

steps.title: Copy from floppy
text: Insert the floppy with the new Interact files and type xcopy A:\*.* . Answer Y to overwrite.

steps.title: Restore the panel
text: Remove the floppy and lock its door. Unplug the HMI power, remove the keyboard and store the pigtail inside the panel. Reconnect power to reboot and refit the cover screws.

documents.title: Bosch capper: intermittent SERCOS communication loss
documents.summary: Alarm 198 Capper SERCOS error during production or hooking, caused by a loose SERCOS RJ45 connector on a drive.
documents.issue: During production or hooking the capper faults with **Alarm 198, Capper SERCOS error**. The Bosch web diagnostic log shows SERCOS errors (E0004020, E00B0179) and devices missing after a certain SERCOS address.
documents.fix: Find the drive where the ring stops. Check the link LEDs on its SERCOS ports. Reseat or replace the loose RJ45 on the hybrid SERCOS cable. Both ports should show L solid and S flashing.

blocks.heading: What the log shows
text: In the example, every device after SERCOS address 16 was missing.

blocks.heading: How it was found
bullets: All SERCOS cables checked. No slip ring fault found and no damaged cables.
The SERCOS cables were tested with an ethernet tester and were OK.
LED indicators were missing on port X7E1 of the drive after the last good address.
A loose connection was found at the drive's control unit connector.
blocks.caption: Observed LED state on the faulty port

steps.title: Find the break
text: From the diagnostic log, find the first missing SERCOS address. Check the ports on the drive before it.

steps.title: Check the LEDs
text: Compare the port LEDs with the Bosch IndraDrive documentation. A healthy port shows L solid and S flashing on both X7E1 and X7E2.

steps.title: Reseat or replace the connector
text: Reseat the RJ45 on the hybrid SERCOS cable. If it will not latch firmly, replace the connector.
steps.caption: Loose hybrid cable SERCOS RJ45

steps.title: Confirm
text: Power up and check both ports show L solid and S flashing, and that all addresses are present.
steps.caption: Connection OK

documents.title: Motor or servo drive: intermittent stop or enable loss
documents.summary: A drive stops or loses its enable with no fault because a high-voltage motor starter contact block is switching a 24 V DC signal.

meta.Status: Fix: replace contact block with 24 V DC relay

documents.issue: The machine powers up, homes and runs, then a drive (servo scroll, conveyor) stops or loses its enable **with no fault** other than the missing enable. After a power cycle it may or may not run.
documents.fix:
Temporary: move the wires to another set of contacts on the block.
Permanent: replace the Allen-Bradley CAT 100 contact block with a suitable 24 V DC relay.

blocks.heading: Cause
text: Some machines use an Allen-Bradley Catalog 100 auxiliary contactor (100-K09DJ400) rated for higher voltage to switch 24 V DC drive enable and stop signals. Its contacts do not reliably make at 24 V DC, so the signal drops out intermittently. It is a component problem, not software, parameters or wiring.

steps.title: How it is wired
text: CR2.1 and CR2.2 close when both disconnects are ON. With CR2.2 closed, the drive enable goes to the scroll drive input 1 (Drive Enable).

steps.title: What was found
text: The normally open contact 5/6 on CR2.2 lost contact intermittently. Moving the wires to the spare contact 13/14 cleared the problem.

steps.title: How it is wired
text: CR3.1 closes when both disconnects are ON, and holds the Stop input of the PowerFlex 525 belt drive ON so it can run.

steps.title: What was found
text: Drive parameters and PLC logic were unchanged from factory. Replacing the CAT 100 block with an IDEC 24 V DC relay fixed it.

documents.title: Fillers: wide fill variation from old flowmeter calibration data
documents.summary: Each head fills consistently but the heads disagree by 0.2% or more, because leftover calibration data from commissioning is still loaded.

meta.Machine: Any filler or monoblock with batching meters

documents.issue: One filling station on its own is consistent and on target, but across all heads the fills are above or below target and the spread is **0.2% of the fill or more** (for a 1000 g fill, more than plus or minus 2 g).
documents.fix: Reset every head's calibration to the factory values, **correction 0** and **scaling 1.0000** (DOSIMASS and DOSIMAG). Run the machine again and calibrate heads only if needed.

blocks.heading: Cause
text: Calibration data from an earlier commissioning was still in the recipe. The correction and scaling factors varied widely from head to head. If all heads had been calibrated for one product, the values would sit in a similar range. Bad data makes the meters dose differently from what they measure.

steps.title: Reset the data
text: Set every head's compensation correction to 0 and scaling factor to 1.0000, and save to the recipe.

steps.title: Check and calibrate
text: Run the machine, run a Quality Control and only calibrate heads that are out of limits. See the flow meter calibration guide.

documents.title: PV-60-S tank pressure overshoots on restart
documents.summary: After stopping tank pressure and lowering the set point, the pressure overshoots on restart because an internal PLC value is not reset.

meta.Machine: Fillers with PV-60-S tank pressure control

documents.issue: With tank pressure **stopped**, the operator changes the pressure preset (for example 3.5 bar to 1 bar). When tank pressure restarts, the commanded output overshoots well above the new set point before settling. Changing the preset while tank pressure is running works normally.
documents.fix: Software change: at tank pressure shutdown, set the internal calculation **Pressure_Output** to 0 as well as the output command **SFW_TankOutput_PSI**.

steps.title: Stop
text: Running at 3.5 bar, tank pressure is stopped. The command (red) drops to 0 and real pressure (pink) falls.

steps.title: Restart at a lower set point
text: The set point (blue) is changed to 1 bar and tank pressure restarted. The command overshoots and real pressure rises above target.

steps.title: Normal
text: Changing the set point while running: command and pressure follow normally.

blocks.heading: Cause
text: When tank pressure stops, the output command is set to 0 bar, but the internal calculation that feeds it keeps its previous value. On restart the old value is used. Not a safety hazard, but the overshoot can be large and affects fill weights.

blocks.heading: Permanent fix
text: In **QT1_PV_60_S**, routine **LD16_TankPressure**, add a MOV of 0 to **Pressure_Output** on the shutdown branch, alongside the existing move to **SFW_TankOutput_PSI**.

documents.title: Bosch servo turrets: spindles stay down after an alarm during hooking
documents.summary: If an alarm interrupts e-cam hooking, the e-cam is left not ready but the machine can still rotate with spindles lowered and hit the bridge.

meta.System: E-cam homing and hooking, PLC alarm 304

documents.issue: After homing, the e-cam is hooked by rotating the turret. If an alarm (for example **Main air valve fault**) stops the machine mid-hooking, followed by **Alarm 126 Bosch MLC2 fault**, then after reset **CAM NOT READY** is red but **no alarm** is active. The machine can return to Idle and rotate with spindles at working height, and they collide with the capper bridge.
documents.fix:
Change the Alarm 304 (E-CAM NOT READY) rung so it is raised in this condition and stops rotation until the operator **aborts** the e-cam and repeats the homing check and hooking.
Until then: after any alarm during hooking, abort the e-cam and re-home before rotating.

steps.title: Homing check
text: E-cam aborted, then Homing Check pressed. Spindles go to working offset ready for hooking.

steps.title: Hooking starts
text: The turret rotates; after the head 1 photocell, the chucks follow the e-cam profile. No Bosch alarms.

steps.title: Alarm during hooking
text: The machine stops for an alarm, here a main air valve fault from a plant air loss, before hooking finishes.

steps.title: MLC2 fault
text: Alarm 126 Bosch MLC2 fault follows; the operator presses E-stop to clear it. The bit E-cam Initialized and Hooked OK is lost.

steps.title: Not ready, but no alarm
text: CAM NOT READY is now red but nothing stops the machine. Rotating now can crash the lowered spindles into the bridge.

blocks.heading: Cause
text: In the original logic (EM40_ServoCapperA, CM50_Capper_Control), Alarm 304 is only raised once the e-cam is hooked. Here it was never hooked, so the alarm never came.

blocks.heading: Fix
text: The rung was changed so Alarm 304 is raised in this condition. The operator must abort the e-cam and re-home; if no further alarm occurs, homing and hooking proceed normally. Check other machines with Bosch servo turrets; it is not known whether Kinetix turrets are affected.

documents.title: Theory of operations: Ronchi monoblock
documents.summary: How the four parts of a Ronchi monoblock work together: product delivery, filling, cap or pump supply and capping.

blocks.heading: The monoblock
text: A monoblock is a rotary volumetric filler and a rotary capper on one base. The two turrets are mechanically connected and run in sync.

blocks.heading: Product delivery
text: Product reaches the filler manifold under pressure. A PID loop in the main PLC holds that pressure. The pressure is measured after the air bleed valve, just before the manifold. The customer can tune the PID settings so the meters see a steady supply, which is what gives accurate doses.

blocks.heading: Filling
text: Each filling station has a mass or magnetic flowmeter, a MAC pilot valve and a pneumatic liquid valve. Product flows from the manifold through the meter, which reports the dosed volume to the filling PLC under the turret. The filling PLC handles nothing but dosing.
The target weight is set once on the HMI and applies to every station. You cannot set a different dose for each head.

blocks.heading: Cap and pump supply
text: An elevator and hopper feed caps or pumps to the sorter. The rotating sorter disc and its change tooling turn each part the right way up. A conveyor keeps a buffer of parts in front of the capper and delivers them to the loading star, which places each one in time with the capping turret and the bottles.

blocks.heading: Capping
text: Each capping head carries a chuck made for that cap or pump. Chucks change quickly, so one capper can run many closures.

Bosch servo motors both screw the closure on and drive the electronic cam that picks up the cap and places it on the bottle. From the HMI you set rotation angles, torque, speed and the steps the head runs: rotate, orient, pre-position, screw and clamp.

documents.title: SCADA technical training, days 1 to 5
documents.summary: The five-day Ronchi Smart Connection (RSC) SCADA course in one guide: hardware and software, the Wonderware Galaxy, panel navigation, online changes, security levels, drivers and debugging, SQL Server recipes and backups, digital manuals and multi-language labels.

meta.Machine: Machines with the RSC SCADA panel (B&R industrial PC)
meta.Software: AVEVA Wonderware System Platform, SQL Server 2014

safety: Always back up the Galaxy and the database before making changes. Never redeploy on a running line without telling the operators: the panel restarts.

blocks.heading: Day 1: What RSC is
text: Ronchi Smart Connection is the SCADA panel: a friendlier operator interface with local storage of variables, digital manuals, local alarm warnings (for example motors), an audit trail of key variables, a log of user operations and a direct link to the recipe server.

rows: B&R industrial PC with panel, UPS-backed supply. Ethernet port 1 to the machine network, port 2 to the internet.
AVEVA Wonderware System Platform: graphics, scripting, runtime and PLC communication
SQL Server 2014: recipes, history of data and user operations, alarms, digital-manual links
From the WW_CLNT virtual machine only. VNC to the industrial PC gives the runtime, not the IDE, unless the PC has a development licence.
Same subnet as the machine: 192.168.10.x for a monoblock, 192.168.20.x for Betel. Pick an address no machine component uses.
RNH-SRV01 monoblock, RNH-SRV02 Betel. Galaxy names follow GLX_<machine number>MB or RR.
Templates for every component (cap feeders, robots…) with their attributes, linked symbols and PLC variable definitions
Every page, popup and toolbar shown on the panel. Each page lists its elements, the page itself and the selected element's properties
The engines. The Galaxy Repository (GR) must be deployed for the runtime to work. Graphic changes need the graphic engine redeployed; template changes need that element redeployed

blocks.heading: Day 2: Panel navigation
bullets: **Toolbar** (on every main page): login, operating mode, PackML state, live alarm and status events, quick settings.
**Navigation bar**: grouped by operating mode, machine element, recipe, layout and statistics.
**Footbar**: shortcuts such as camera links.
Square fields only display; buttons open popups or run scripts; rounded fields take input.
A **dot** beside a field means its value is saved in the recipe.

steps.title: Add a variable
steps.text: In Deployment open GLX_…/GR/EngMac_Monoblock/MONOBLOCK/MB_MacRoot/_MB_Customer. Every variable added after machine set-up goes in _MB_Customer. Click Add, fill in the fields, save, then redeploy _MB_Customer if the GR is deployed.

steps.title: Add a graphic element
steps.text: In the Graphic Toolbox open the page (for example Gt_MB_FillA). Copy a similar element, rename it in the element list, change its labels and variable reference. Take care what you copy. Redeploy the graphic engine IntViewApp01 and restart the runtime.

steps.title: Show or hide an element
steps.text: The master Galaxy has elements for most options, hidden when not used. To hide: Transparency 80, Enabled False, Visible False. To show: Transparency 0, Enabled True, Visible True. Some visibility is driven by animations instead, and animations override object properties. Redeploy the graphic engine afterwards.

blocks.heading: Day 3: Security levels
text: Users log in as Operator I/II, Maintenance I/II or Supervisor I/II. Each kind of field (basic control, parameter edit, counter reset, set point, recipe edit) is tied to an InTouch variable such as MemD_AccLvl_Modify_CTRL or MemD_AccLvl_SetPoint_EDIT. Fields grey out automatically when the login does not meet that level.
To add a set point editable from Maintenance I upward, use MemD_AccLvl_SetPoint_EDIT in the field's animation or custom properties, then check it in the runtime.

steps.title: Back up the Galaxy
steps.text: Galaxy Database Manager → right-click the Galaxy → Backup → Yes → choose path and name → Save.

steps.title: Manage drivers
steps.text: ABCIP for Rockwell PLCs, SIDIR for Siemens, MBTCP for Modbus. Right-click → Activate (auto start after reboot) or Deactivate. Restart a driver after an unclean PC shutdown, lost PLC or Modbus communication, or Ethernet changes on the PC.

steps.title: Debug with Log Viewer
steps.text: The log lists every error, warning and status event, for example expired licences or a PLC not communicating. Export with Action → Messages → Export as an .aaLGX file to send to Ronchi Italy.

blocks.heading: Day 4: SQL Server
text: There is one database per machine (named RN_<machine number>MB or RR). Tables hold recipes, user and login logs, alarms and digital-manual links. Stored procedures, launched from IDE scripts, insert, update and delete recipe values.

steps.title: Check a recipe saved
steps.text: Right-click dbo.Ar_MB_Prod_Main → Select Top 200 Rows and find the recipe. The other MB tables work the same way.

steps.title: Back up the database
steps.text: Right-click the database → Tasks → Back Up. Remove the existing path, click Add and choose a new one. Always end the file name with .bak or the backup cannot be used. Under Media Options choose Overwrite all existing backups, then OK. This saves every recipe and its values.

steps.title: Copy the files
steps.text: Copy the machine's digital-manual folder to C:\Ronchi\Projects\Digital_Manuals\ManFull on the B&R PC.

steps.title: Load the links
steps.text: Open the Scada Digital Man Matrix workbook for the machine and copy the URL_DigMan_OFFLINE column. In SQL Server edit the top 200 rows of dbo.SYS_MB_DigMan_Code and paste into URL_DigMan_OFFLINE.

steps.title: Update the Galaxy
steps.text: In the IDE open $INI_Cmn (or $INI_MB on newer machines) in the Template Toolbox and replace the three monoblock links with the ones at the end of the workbook.

steps.title: Map the value
steps.text: Open page Gt_MB_ProdRecipes → right-click the grey area → Scripts. In _34_Save_To_DB_CustomerAUX assign a spare slot, for example liInt_01 = _MB_Customer.SDR_Test.

steps.title: Write it back to the PLC
steps.text: If the page has script _Write_To_PLC_CustomerAux, replace lsAuxToDelete in the Int_01 row with your variable. If not, open MB_RcpMngt_AutoDwnd in Deployment and do the same there.

steps.title: Name the column
steps.text: In Gt_MB_ProdRecipes edit the script of the Custom button so the row reads Int_01 AS 'SDR_Test'.

steps.title: Link the dot
steps.text: Point the field's dot at Tables → Attributes → gsActualValue. Save, redeploy everything and test by saving a new recipe.

blocks.heading: Day 5: Multi-language labels
text: Every new label needs its translations entered by hand. Add the label, switch the graphic's display language, type the translation, repeat for every language, save, redeploy the graphic engine and check each language in the runtime.

blocks.heading: Support
text: Software questions for the Ronchi Italy SCADA team go to ute.sw@ronchi.it. Send the Log Viewer export and a Galaxy backup with the request.

documents.title: SCADA software: master to job, PC restore
documents.summary: How to build a job's RSC SCADA from the Ronchi master, back it up, and restore or rebuild the industrial PC on site: re-imaging, licence, database, Galaxy, drivers, deploy, recipe variables and digital manuals.

meta.Machine: Machines with the RSC SCADA panel (B&R industrial PC)
meta.Software: AVEVA Wonderware System Platform, SQL Server 2014

safety: Undeploy the Galaxy before any restore. Always save application backups in the undeployed state. Logins for SQL Server, the IDE and the PC are Ronchi-only: get the login from the Ronchi service lead; never give it to the customer.

rows: Recipes and alarm data, alarm and trend history, operator events, MES and batch data
Develops the SCADA and serves the runtime on the panel. Needs SQL Server installed

blocks.heading: Part 1: Build a job from the master (in the office)

steps.title: Copy the master backups
steps.text: Copy the master database (.bak) to C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL14.MSSQLSERVER\MSSQL\Backup\ and the master SCADA (.cab) to C:\Program Files (x86)\ArchestrA\Framework\Bin\BackupGalaxies on the virtual machine.

steps.title: Restore the database
steps.text: In SQL Server Management Studio log in with SQL Server Authentication (get the login from the Ronchi service lead; never give it to the customer). Right-click Databases → Restore Database → Device → Add → pick the .bak. Rename the target to the job, for example RN_<job>MB. Tick the overwrite options only if overwriting. Wait for Restore successful.

steps.title: Create the Galaxy
steps.text: In the IDE create a new Galaxy from the master .cab.

steps.title: Set user passwords
steps.text: Galaxy → Configure → Security with no object open. Set op1 and op2 passwords to the job number. The other users' passwords are in the user configuration workbook on the Ronchi Italy server.

steps.title: Set global constants
steps.text: In $INI_Cmn set simulation, machine type, local folders, start-up language, MES present, digital manuals present and the job database name.

steps.title: Trim the deployment
steps.text: Drag engines the job does not need into Unassigned Host.

steps.title: Configure the monoblock
steps.text: In $INI_MB set the head counts (pages resize automatically) and recipe and washing constants. If there are more than two feeders, elevators, fillers or cappers, enable the commented sections in the Gt_MB_ProdRecipes scripts. Extra instances (FillerB, CapperB, feeders C/D…) are ready in the AUX engine: drag them in, then build their graphics. If only one feeder is fitted, check whether CFA is caps or pumps; the master assumes caps.

steps.title: Set the driver
steps.text: Server Name ABCIP for Rockwell or SIDIR for Siemens.

steps.title: Edit the pages
steps.text: Check Gt_MB_HomeScreen, the layout pages (motors, photocells, proximities, sensors), Gt_MB_FillA, Gt_MB_CapA, the machine cams page and Gt_MB_ProdINIT (32 cam descriptions), the maintenance motor pages, format change and conveyor data. Delete controls and motors that are not fitted.

steps.title: Betel only
steps.text: Set $INI_Betel. Import the hardware files for B&R, Rockwell or Siemens: first the .csv with Galaxy → Import → Galaxy Load (Only update changed attributes), then the two .aaPKG files with Import Object(s) (Overwrite objects regardless of configuration version).

blocks.heading: Part 2: Save the final backups
text: Back up three things: the database, the Galaxy and the recipes. Save the application undeployed.

steps.title: Database
steps.text: From the WW_CLNT VM open SQL Server Management Studio, expand the server and Databases, right-click RN_<job> → Tasks → Back Up. Remove every existing destination, Add a new file named exactly like the database with .bak, for example RN_<job>MB.bak. Under Media Options choose Overwrite all existing backup sets. The file is saved on the B&R PC, not the VM.

steps.title: Galaxy
steps.text: VNC from the VM to the B&R PC and close the runtime. In the Management Console, Galaxy Database Manager → right-click the Galaxy → Backup → Yes. Keep the suggested GLX_ name and save next to the database backup.

steps.title: Copy to the server
steps.text: From the VM open \\RNH-SRV01\c$ (monoblock) or \\RNH-SRV02\c$ (Betel), copy both files to the job folder on the server, then restart the runtime.

steps.title: Recipes
steps.text: On a laptop with Excel and Power Query (not the VM), open the recipe export template for MB, Betel or batches. Enter the connection parameters. Set Query Options → Privacy → Always ignore privacy levels, and in Trust Center enable ActiveX, VBA macros and all data connections. Data → Refresh All, log in with the SQL login, accept an unencrypted connection, click through errors for empty tables. Check the sheets hold recipe data and save the file to the job folder.

blocks.heading: Part 3: Restore or rebuild the PC on site

steps.title: Re-image (recommended)
steps.text: Plug in the boot USB and the image drive, monitor (DVI), keyboard and mouse. Press F11 at start-up and pick UEFI: Generic Flash Disk. Choose Troubleshoot → Advanced → System Image Recovery → Windows 10 and pick the image: RNH-SRV01 monoblock, RNH-SRV02 Betel + PickMaster, RNH-PickMaster for PickMaster only. Untick the image drive, Finish.

steps.title: Fix display scaling
steps.text: After re-imaging set Display Settings → scale to 100% (it may come back at 125%, making the graphics too large).

steps.title: Activate the licence
steps.text: Connect the PC's free eth2 port to a DHCP network and reach it by RDP or VNC (monoblock 192.168.10.55 / RNH-SRV01; robot 192.168.150.21 / RNH-SRV02; PickMaster 192.168.150.20; get the login from the Ronchi service lead; never give it to the customer). Open the firewall for internet, extract the job's licence file from the job folder on the server and activate it. Delete any annual development licence (.bin) found afterwards, because it overrides the job licence.

steps.title: Restore the database
steps.text: Copy the job .bak to the B&R PC via \\RNH-SRV01\c$. In SQL Server Management Studio connect to RNH-SRV01 or RNH-SRV02, restore as in Part 1 and check the database name matches the job.

steps.title: Configure SQL users
steps.text: In the restored database open Programmability, run the user auto-configuration stored procedure and check the return value is 0.

steps.title: Create the Galaxy
steps.text: Copy the job .cab to C:\Program Files (x86)\ArchestrA\Framework\Bin\BackupGalaxies on the industrial PC (not the VM). In the IDE click New Galaxy, GR node RNH-SRV01 or RNH-SRV02, and pick the backup.

steps.title: Activate drivers
steps.text: In the Management Console activate (auto start after reboot) the drivers this machine uses.

steps.title: Deploy
steps.text: Connect the IDE to the Galaxy (get the login from the Ronchi service lead; never give it to the customer). In Deployment right-click GR → Deploy with default settings. There must be no errors and no yellow markers left.

steps.title: Start the runtime
steps.text: First time only: open InTouch Application Manager, select the row and click Windows Viewer. It then starts automatically at every boot.

blocks.heading: Add a recipe variable
text: The master has spare recipe slots: 10 booleans, 10 integers, 10 reals and 10 strings, each with an orange dot editor.

steps.title: Link the slot
steps.text: In the Gt_MB_ProdRecipes (or Gt_RR_ProdRecipes) page scripts link your variable to a spare local, for example lbBit_01 = Instance.NewBool.

steps.title: Write it to the PLC
steps.text: In the write-to-PLC script replace lsAuxToDelete with your variable. On older masters this script is in the deployed object MB_RcpMngt_AutoDwnd.

steps.title: Name the column
steps.text: In the Action Scripts of btnCustom rename the column, for example Bit_01 AS 'NewBool'.

steps.title: Configure the editor
steps.text: Set the editor's wizard options and custom properties for the variable.

steps.title: Check it was sold
steps.text: Check the order or ask sales whether digital manuals were sold. If not, skip this.

steps.title: Get the files
steps.text: Check the manuals department has prepared them and they are on the server. Copy the whole folder to C:\Ronchi\Projects\Digital_Manuals\ManFull on the B&R PC.

steps.title: Update references
steps.text: Using the manuals department's workbook, update the link column of the digital-manual table in SQL Server and the $INI_Cmn constants for the format change procedure.

documents.title: Electrical axes and PackML (Rockwell and Siemens)
documents.summary: How the ELECTRICAL_AXIS block gears a monoblock carousel to an upstream machine, and how Ronchi PackML programs are laid out on Rockwell and Siemens monoblocks.

meta.Machine: EXACTA monoblocks with servo main motor

blocks.heading: ELECTRICAL_AXIS block
text: This block runs the carousel main motor either geared to a master axis (electrical axis) or at its own speed. Use it when the monoblock must follow an encoder on another machine.
Master and slave axes must be rotary with a 360° (one-step) modulo. The slave motor encoder must be absolute multi-turn.
If re-phasing needs more than 30°, the block asks for confirmation through I_AckRephasing. Homing or referencing of the master axis is done by other blocks, which report through I_MasterSyncOK.
blocks.caption: ELECTRICAL_AXIS block

rows: Tag name of the block instance
Master axis (encoder on the other machine)
Disable delay after an emergency stop. Must be longer than the Pilz relay delay
Mode: ON electrical axis (gear), OFF speed
Master position valid. TRUE at once for an absolute single-turn encoder; for an encoder on another machine, TRUE when its value is valid
Electrical axis mode: starts homing and phasing. Speed mode: starts the motor
Acknowledge to start re-phasing. Set to 1 permanently to skip the acknowledge
Re-phasing speed in electrical axis mode (BPM). 30 BPM suggested
Slave axis fault. Add to SA_MMOT_EMER_STP
Powered, homed. If false in error, add to SA_MMOT_STP
Ready. If false in error, add to SA_MMOT_STBY_STP
Master axis fault. Add to SA_MMOT_EMER_STP

blocks.heading: PackML program layout
bullets: **PackML Manager**: the main AOI (Rockwell) or FB (Siemens) that runs the PackML state machine.
**PackTags**: the standard data exchange with the line controller.
**Customer OEE/OMAC exchange**: some customers define their own data structures for line data; these are added on top of PackTags.

**Events**: Alarms are machine stops, Warnings are feeder events, Status Events are messages. All three use the same message structure. See the tag naming scheme and master alarm list for IDs and categories.

blocks.heading: Differences from the older P&G-style PackML
bullets: HMI tags are standard tags.
Recipes are no longer stored in the PLC.
The HMI keeps its own alarm texts; it does not read alarm text from the PLC.
Languages for alarms, tags and pages are handled entirely in FactoryTalk on the HMI.

documents.title: Cognex camera training
documents.summary: How to connect to the capper's Cognex In-Sight cameras, record production images, and tune the spout orientation and spout check cameras to cut false rejects.

meta.Machine: Cappers with Cognex In-Sight cap cameras

blocks.heading: Before you start
text: Single cappers usually have two cameras and double cappers three. Screw caps (spigot type) only need a presence check; spout caps must also be oriented, so they use an orientation camera and a check camera.
Make changes with a laptop connected so you can record images during production and see exactly what the camera sees when it rejects.

steps.title: Plug in
steps.text: Connect an Ethernet cable from the laptop to the service socket on the main Ronchi panel.

steps.title: Set the IP address
steps.text: In the laptop's adapter settings set a fixed IPv4 address in the camera network, 192.168.11.x with mask 255.255.255.0. Make sure only one adapter on the laptop has a 192.168.11.x address.

steps.title: Open In-Sight Explorer
steps.text: The cameras on the network appear automatically. Double-click a camera to open it in spreadsheet view.

steps.title: Find the jobs and filmstrip
steps.text: The left pane lists the jobs stored in the camera. The filmstrip at the bottom holds the last 20 images.
steps.caption: Jobs stored in the camera

callouts.label: Note
callouts.text: You cannot edit a past image while viewing it from the sensor. Save the images to the laptop first, then work on them.

steps.title: Make folders
steps.text: Create a folder on the laptop desktop for the recordings.

steps.title: Set record and playback folders
steps.text: Image → Record/Playback Options: set the Record folder and the Playback folder.

steps.title: Set the filmstrip folder
steps.text: Go offline (Sensor → Online off), then Sensor → Filmstrip settings and choose where the filmstrip is saved. Going offline clears the last 20 images from the camera.

steps.title: Record during production
steps.text: With the machine running, press the red record button, or press Freeze and save the filmstrip.

steps.title: Review
steps.text: Go offline and select PC on the filmstrip to browse the saved images. Find the cause, fix it, then put the camera back online.

blocks.heading: Camera 1: spout orientation
text: This camera finds the black mark on the cap inside a ring-shaped search area and measures its angle from zero. It sends the angle to the Bosch capping motor, which turns the spout to the right position.

steps.title: Position compensation
steps.text: Options → Position Compensation centres the search on the cap so the ring area follows the cap. Set it with the Region window.

steps.title: Presence window
steps.text: The Presence window checks there is a cap on the chuck.

steps.title: Ring search area
steps.text: The ring (can circumference) must cover the band where the black mark can be. If the mark is outside it, the camera will fail.

rows: Camera triggers too early or late
Adjust the capper orientation camera cam point on the HMI cam page to centre the cap
Edge tool threshold or mode wrong, or poor lighting
Offline, double-click the second Edge cell in the spreadsheet. Set the threshold and choose Strongest Edge to ignore light noise. Check the light settings
Close the ring so its start and end meet; a mark sitting at the gap fails
Compensation edge not centred or not clearly visible
Make sure the first Edge (centring) tool sees a clear, well-defined edge and the cap stays inside its area

blocks.heading: Camera 2: spout check
text: This camera checks the spout ended up in the right position. It works like camera 1: centre on the cap, draw the ring, and check the black mark falls inside an angle window set in the Options menu.

rows: Make the centring edge clear and well defined
Widen the angle limits in Options to the real tolerance

documents.title: Tuning the filler pressure PID
documents.summary: What each setting on the EXACTA product pressure PID page does, good starting values, and a step-by-step method to tune a steady fill pressure.

meta.Machine: EXACTA fillers with pump-fed product supply

blocks.heading: The PID page
text: Settings are on the left; the pressure trend is on the right, with the pressure preset and pump stop delay underneath. The aim is a steady actual pressure (magenta line) as close as possible to the preset (blue line).
Each setting has three values: Standard (during production), Start ramp and Stop ramp.
blocks.caption: PID parameter page

rows: How hard the pump reacts to a pressure error at the manifold. Higher gain = stronger reaction.
Standard 15% to 100% of the pressure preset: 0.15 at 1 bar, 0.75 at 5 bar. Start ramp higher than standard; stop ramp higher than start.
How quickly the controller removes a lasting error. Works against the gain.
Standard 3 to 5 s depending on speed: about 5 s at 150 BPM, 3 s at 250 BPM. Start and stop 0.01 to 0.75 s.
Dead band either side of the preset where the pump speed is not changed. Too small makes the PID hunt; too large allows a bigger error.
Start at 0.03 bar. Never above 0.10 bar for standard, start or stop.
Time used at start and stop so the first and last bottles fill correctly.
The fill time of one bottle, for example 6 s.
Raises the preset by a percentage while its timer runs at start-up, to cover the pressure dip when the valves first open.
Not part of the standard set-up. Leave the timer at 0.0 s to disable.
How long the multiplier is applied.
A few seconds longer than the start ramp if used.

blocks.heading: Reading the trend

rows: Gain too high and/or integral time too low
Gain too low and/or integral time too high

text: Low-pressure products: low gain (about 15% of the preset) and higher start/stop ramps (about 50%). High-pressure products: higher gain (about 50%) and lower start/stop ramps (about 15%).

steps.title: Start clean
steps.text: Set a low proportional gain and set integral time and hysteresis band to zero.

steps.title: Tune the gain
steps.text: Double the gain until the pressure starts to oscillate, then halve it. Watch and repeat until it is stable.

steps.title: Tune the integral
steps.text: Set the minimum integral time and double it until it oscillates, then halve it. Watch and repeat.

steps.title: Set the band
steps.text: Set the hysteresis band to 0.03 bar, watch over time and raise it only if needed (maximum 0.10 bar).

steps.title: One at a time
steps.text: Work on gain, then integral, then band, in that order. Do not change two at once: they work against each other.

documents.title: Filler zero point and bottle presence timing
documents.summary: How to check the EXACTA filler's mechanical zero, the head 1 photocell and CAM1 so every bottle is detected and filled.
safety: Jog with all guards closed. Lock out before reaching under the turret to adjust the encoder coupling.

steps.title: Set jog speed
steps.text: Set the jog speed to 50 BPM.

steps.title: Find mechanical zero
steps.text: Jog slowly while watching the zero pointer under the filler turret, viewed from the rear of the machine inside the lower base. The 0 mark is on the side of the carousel plate that carries the filler PLC.

steps.title: Stop on zero
steps.text: Stop when the pointer lines up with the 0 mark.

steps.title: Check the bottle presence photocell
steps.text: The bottle presence photocell, usually under the infeed star (on some fillers in the scroll), must be on the centre of the bottle that head 1 will fill.

steps.title: Check the head 1 photocell
steps.text: The head 1 photocell rotates with the filler; its reflector is on the base frame. It should be on the first third of the reflector, just before the centre in the direction of rotation.

steps.title: Set CAM1
steps.text: CAM1 should go high when the head 1 cell is at, or just after, the centre of the reflector. Zero the encoder by turning its coupling while watching the CAM screen on the HMI.

callouts.label: Why it matters
callouts.text: The head 1 photocell must turn on before CAM1. If not, alarm 373 appears after three consecutive turns past the cell, or bottles are not filled because bottle presence never reaches the filler PLC.

documents.title: Bosch linear cam simulator
documents.summary: How the Ronchi linear cam simulator workbook checks a capper spindle's up-and-down cam profile before it is loaded into the Bosch drives, with an example 16-point profile.

meta.Machine: Cappers with Bosch Rexroth linear ECAM spindles

blocks.heading: What the simulator does
text: Each spindle's vertical position (Y, mm) is defined against turret angle (X, degrees) by 16 points over one 360° turn. Between points the simulator fits a motion law (5th-order polynomial by default; 3rd and 7th order, sinusoid, cycloidal and modified trapezoid are also available) and calculates speed and acceleration.
It then checks the profile against the motor limits at the set production speed and shows **MOTION CHECK OK** or a fault. Always get OK before typing the points into the HMI cam page.

blocks.heading: Example profile
bullets: Points 1–6: spindle up, waiting for the cap.
Point 7–8: down 82 mm to pick the cap.
Points 9–10: up to 37 mm to carry the cap over the bottle.
Points 11–13: down to 156–159 mm to screw the cap on, held for most of the turn.
Points 14–16: back up to zero before the next cycle.

blocks.heading: Good practice
bullets: Change one point at a time and re-check the motion after each change.
Keep the steepest moves away from the pick-up and screwing zones.
Save a copy of the workbook with the machine number and date before handing over.

documents.title: Alarm 275 stops the filler and cannot be cleared
documents.summary: A wrong alarm bit on the counter reset makes alarm 275 (consecutive low fill errors) impossible to clear on some Ronchi fillers.
documents.issue:
Alarm 275, consecutive low filling errors, stops the machine. It is a category 3 alarm, so the machine cannot restart, and the operator **cannot reset it**.
You may also see the consecutive rejects setting on the filler parameters page drop from 99 (maximum) to 3.
documents.fix:
Update the PLC logic so the counter reset uses Alarm 275 instead of Alarm 191 (see below).
Until the update is loaded, use one of the temporary workarounds.

blocks.heading: Cause
text: The reset of the consecutive filling error counter is tied to the wrong alarm flag. In fast task **T02**, Filler fast task **EM40FT**, Filling Error control **CM21**, **Rung 5**, the lowest branch uses **Alarm 191** (movable fiddle) instead of Alarm 275.

steps.title: Raise the consecutive error limit
text: On the filler parameters page, set the number of consecutive filling errors back up, to a maximum of 99.

steps.title: Or cycle the level control
text: Turn the liquid level control off, then back on, and restart the machine.

steps.title: Correct Rung 5
text: In T02 > EM40FT > CM21, Rung 5, lowest branch: change **Alarm191** to **Alarm275**. Download the change and save the program.
steps.caption: Rung 5 after the correction

callouts.label: Who
callouts.text: Logic changes are made by Ronchi America service or a trained controls engineer. Contact Ronchi America service to schedule the update.

documents.title: Filling and capping speed formulas
documents.summary: Four formulas to work out filler output and the minimum capping spindle speed for a given line speed.

steps.title: Active fill zone
text: H = total number of filling heads. N = heads that do not fill between bottle infeed and exit (typically 6, or 5 on large-pitch fillers). Z = heads in the active fill zone.

callouts.label: Example
callouts.text: A 40-head large-pitch filler: 40 − 5 = 35 heads in the active fill zone.

steps.title: Filling speed
text: F = fill time per bottle in seconds. Z = heads in the active fill zone. BPM = bottles per minute.

steps.title: Capping time per pitch
